catalogTitle: “וצדיק באמונתו יחיה” - The Mitzvah of the Last Generation

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that Habakkuk placed the whole Torah on the one mitzvah of emunah because the last generation, the 'heel' of Adam HaRishon, must concentrate its strength on emunah, which is its special mission.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the Gemara in Makkos that the nevi'im reduced the 613 mitzvos until Habakkuk placed the whole Torah on one: 'the tzaddik lives by his emunah.' This does not free anyone from the other mitzvos; it means a small generation must concentrate on one mitzvah. To explain, he brings the Midrash that all souls were contained in Adam HaRishon, and that the generations together form one body. The generation of the desert was the head, devoted to Torah; later generations with the Beis HaMikdash were the heart, the masters of tefillah, led by Moshe Rabbeinu and David HaMelech respectively. Our generation is the heel: low, without sensitivity, in the dark. The Rav also warns that machlokes can spoil a year fit for Mashiach, as the Chasam Sofer said of an earlier generation. Every soul has a mission, known by a strong desire for it and by the obstacles the Satan puts in its way. Today's mission is emunah, which is why the whole world now works against it.

en: Habakkuk's placing the Torah on emunah does not mean one may drop the other mitzvos; it means the last generation must concentrate on this one mitzvah.
All souls were contained in Adam HaRishon, each attached to a particular limb, and a person functions according to the place his soul came from.
The generations together form one body: the generation of the desert is the head, the generations of the Beis HaMikdash are the heart, and our generation is the heel.
Like the heel, our generation lacks sensitivity and stays in the dark, which is why there is so much blindness and so many Jews going astray.
Every soul is sent down on a particular mission, recognized by two signs: a strong desire for it and the obstacles that make it hard.
Since the mission of today is emunah, the Satan has arranged the whole world to take emunah away.

title.en: Habakkuk's one mitzvah and Adam HaRishon's soul

summary.en: The Rav brings the Gemara in Makkos on how the nevi'im reduced the mitzvos until Habakkuk placed the Torah on emunah, and explains that this means concentrating on one mitzvah, since earlier great souls could give themselves to every mitzvah and we are small. He then brings the Midrash that all souls were in Adam HaRishon, attached to different limbs, and that the generations form one such body.

title.en: The head and the heart of the generations

summary.en: The Rav explains that the generation of the desert was the head, a congregation of Torah and intellect led by Moshe Rabbeinu, while the generations of the Beis HaMikdash were the heart, the masters of tefillah led by David HaMelech. A person from the head or the heart can choose to turn that strength to Torah or tefillah, or to other fields; the hands are perhaps the givers of tzedakah.

title.en: Our generation is the heel

summary.en: The Rav says our generation is the heel of Adam HaRishon. He interrupts to warn that the machlokes now prevalent may spoil a year fit for Mashiach, as the Chasam Sofer said of the great generation of the Yaavetz and Rabbi Yonasan Eybeschutz. Then he explains that like the sole of the foot, our generation has no sensitivity and is always in the dark, hence the blindness and the Jews going astray.

title.en: The mitzvah of the last generation

summary.en: The Rav explains that the Gemara's name for the last generation, 'ikvesa deMeshicha', carries the sense of the heel and of shame, and that it is for this generation that Habakkuk placed everything on emunah. He says one must live with emunah, learn, think and talk about it, and introduces the idea that every soul has a mission the Satan tries to block.

title.en: Two signs of one's mission; the war on emunah

summary.en: The Rav gives two signs of a person's mission: a strong desire, as every creature desires what it needs, and obstacles placed by the Satan, as with rising early to learn and daven. Since today's mission is emunah, the Satan has turned the whole world against it; he tells how the Ba'al Shem Tov left a wagon whose driver showed no faith, and says that having no belief at all is worse than false belief.

catalogTitle: המשך ה' לא גבה לבי

oneLiner.en: Continuing with Tehillim 131, the Rav explains David HaMelech's humility and contentment, contrasts the inner purpose behind the splendor of true tzaddikim with the craving to show off, and draws from Shimi ben Gera's curse and from Tehillim 132 how David accepted everything from Hashem while toiling for Klal Yisrael.

abstract.en: The Rav reads Tehillim 131, 'Hashem, my heart was not haughty', as the words of a king who was the great anav, alongside Moshe and Avraham. He tells how the Bluzhever Rav never lifted his eyes above the small aron kodesh and so never saw a broken mechitzah. He explains that tzaddikim of the house of David, like the Ruzhiner, conducted themselves with royal splendor for the honor of Heaven while being truly lowly, unlike Achashverosh's feast, made only to display wealth, a klipah he sees in today's luxury. He urges contentment in one's spiritual level, describes a person as a weaned child who trusts that what he lacks he does not need, and praises accepting disgrace as atonement. David's silence before Shimi ben Gera made him the fourth leg of the Divine chariot and brought about Purim. Finally he begins Tehillim 132: David's toil to find the place of the Beis HaMikdash.

en: David HaMelech, though a king, was the great anav, one of the three role models of humility of Klal Yisrael with Moshe and Avraham.
The royal splendor of true tzaddikim from the house of David had an inner purpose of kavod shamayim, while they themselves took nothing from this world.
Spending on luxury in order to be seen is the klipah of Achashverosh, and the Rav says it arouses jealousy among the nations.
A person should know his level, be content with it and not reach for greatness beyond him, even in avodas Hashem.
Like a weaned child with its mother, a Jew trusts that what he needs Hashem gives him, and what he lacks is a sign he does not need it.
Disgrace atones for sins without sickness or poverty, so one should thank Hashem for it.
By bearing Shimi ben Gera's curses in silence as decreed from Heaven, David became the fourth leg of the Divine chariot and merited Purim through Mordechai, Shimi's descendant.

title.en: David the king as the great anav

summary.en: The Rav reads 'Hashem, my heart was not haughty' and explains that David, a king, did not seek great things. He brings the Chasam Sofer's instruction to his children and the words of Moshe, Avraham and David as the three models of humility.

title.en: The Bluzhever Rav and the broken mechitzah

summary.en: The Rav tells how the Shinover Rav, visiting the Bluzhever Rav, asked why the women's mechitzah had a broken hole, and the Bluzhever answered that he never lifted his eyes above the low aron kodesh. This illustrates 'my eyes were not lofty'.

title.en: Royal splendor of the house of David

summary.en: The Rav describes the legendary wealth of the Ruzhiner, who said at his passing that he had no pleasure from this world, and explains that souls of the house of David must carry royalty while being truly humble. He tells of the Ruzhiner standing barefoot in the cold at Kiddush Levanah in soleless shoes, and brings Rebbi's wealthy table from the Gemara.

title.en: Achashverosh's feast and the urge to display

summary.en: The Rav distinguishes the inner intent of true tzaddikim from the show of Achashverosh, whose feast was made to display his wealth and his queen. He calls today's growing luxury, ever finer menorahs and taller shtreimels, a klipah of showing off.

title.en: Wealth without display

summary.en: The Rav says comfort for wealthy Jews is fine, but luxury that dazzles the eye arouses the nations' jealousy, as the Shelah and the Chasam Sofer cry out. He shows that an extra million and a half spent on luxury gives pleasure for only two or three weeks.

title.en: Content with one's level, like a weaned child

summary.en: The Rav applies 'I did not walk in great things' to spiritual life: one should strive according to his own abilities, not envy another's level, and recognize that greater levels come from Hashem. He then explains the second verse, the weaned child who trusts its mother, linking it to 'Hashem is my shepherd, I shall not lack'.

title.en: Equanimity toward honor and disgrace

summary.en: The Rav brings the Chovos HaLevavos on the trait of equanimity, where honor and disgrace are the same, and stresses that it is a level for great tzaddikim. Still, everyone can stop chasing honor and see disgrace as an atonement that spares sickness and poverty, for which one should thank Hashem.

title.en: Shimi ben Gera and the fourth leg of the chariot

summary.en: The Rav tells how David, fleeing Avshalom, forbade Yoav to kill Shimi ben Gera, saying Hashem told him to curse, though Shimi was a rebel against the kingdom. Citing the Tomer Devorah, he says that at that moment David became the fourth leg of the Divine chariot, and that sparing Shimi brought Mordechai and Purim.

title.en: Remember for David all his affliction

summary.en: The Rav begins Tehillim 132: David prepared for the Beis HaMikdash though his son would build it, and his foundations still stand. Hashem remembers all his suffering, for the Satan opposes one who strives for good, and David swore not to rest until he found the place Yaakov had designated.

catalogTitle: להנוסעים לארץ ישראל - מעלת וקדושת הארץ

oneLiner.en: Speaking to those about to travel, the Rav explains that Eretz Yisroel is the Shabbos of the world and that one must prepare for it, long for it and work to merit it.

abstract.en: Speaking to people about to travel to Eretz Yisroel, the Rav describes the land's greatness and how to approach it. Eretz Yisroel is the root of the world as Rosh Hashana is of the year; it is the Shabbos of the world, and Yerushalayim is the Shabbos of Eretz Yisroel. The Torah was given for this land, and a Jew there receives a higher neshama, so both good and bad grow stronger. One must therefore prepare to enter it as one prepares for Shabbos: not as a tourist, but with holiness, longing and tefillah, knowing that the yetzer hara there is greater. He brings stories of Reb Mendel Vitebsker, the Bas Ayin and the Ohr HaChaim, the Chasam Sofer on Moshe Rabbeinu's last tefillah, and closes with Yerushalayim, the Kosel and a call to use the opportunity well.

en: Eretz Yisroel is the starting point and root of the world, as Rosh Hashana is of the year; it is the Shabbos of the world, and Yerushalayim is the Shabbos of Eretz Yisroel.
The Torah was made for Eretz Yisroel, and the land does not tolerate sin the way other lands do.
A Jew who comes to Eretz Yisroel receives a higher neshama, as on Shabbos, so a tzaddik becomes greater and a rasha worse.
One cannot enter Eretz Yisroel casually; it requires preparation of holiness, just as one must prepare for Shabbos and the Yamim Tovim.
A healthy Jew longs for Eretz Yisroel as a healthy body has appetite; lacking that longing is a sign that something is wrong.
One can be in Eretz Yisroel and not merit it; meriting it takes tefillah and a struggle with obstacles and a greater yetzer hara.
A tefillah in Eretz Yisroel, and above all in Yerushalayim at the Kosel, is far greater than one elsewhere.

title.en: Eretz Yisroel, the Shabbos of the world

summary.en: The Rav opens with the passuk that Hashem's eyes are always on Eretz Yisroel: as Rosh Hashana is the root of the year, the land is the starting point of the world and its Shabbos, and Yerushalayim is the Shabbos of the land. He speaks of the land's special shemirah, says that learning or sinning there carries the weight of Shabbos, and brings the Chasam Sofer that a tzaddik grows greater there and a rasha worse.

title.en: The land of the Torah and a higher neshama

summary.en: Bringing the Ramban and Rashi, the Rav shows that the Torah was made for Eretz Yisroel and that the land cannot bear sin. He explains that a Jew there receives a higher neshama, like the neshama yeseira of Shabbos, citing the Chesed L'Avraham and Yaakov Avinu's angels, and uses the image of a high-voltage wire to explain why both a tzaddik and a rasha grow there.

title.en: Preparing to enter, as for Shabbos

summary.en: The Rav links Shabbos to Yerushalayim through the bracha of Boneh Yerushalayim in bentching, then teaches that one may not enter Eretz Yisroel casually: the people had milah before crossing with Yehoshua, and a Midrash sets conditions of holiness for entering. Just as no one can step into Shabbos straight from a ballgame, one must prepare on Erev Shabbos, each according to his root.

title.en: Ringed by water; being there without meriting it

summary.en: The Rav brings the Ramak that Eretz Yisroel is surrounded by water on all four sides, so entering it is like going to the mikveh before Shabbos. A tourist bathing in the Dead Sea has nothing of the land; just as one who skips the tefillos, kiddush and seudos has no share in Shabbos, one can be in Eretz Yisroel and not merit it.

title.en: Holier than a shul; a longing like for Shabbos

summary.en: The Rav says one cannot play around with Eretz Yisroel: its kedusha exceeds that of a beis haknesses, where one turns one's heart toward the land, so it is the King's palace and not a place for fun. He brings the Sefer Chareidim that a Jew must long for the land, as erliche Yidden long for Shabbos all week.

title.en: A healthy Jew longs for the land

summary.en: The Rav explains that Eretz Yisroel, like Shabbos, is called 'chemdah', and that Hashem gave the land He loves to the people He loves. As a healthy body has appetite, a healthy Jew longs for Torah, tefillah and the land: amoraim kissed its stones and rolled in its dust, the Rambam brings this as halacha, and David HaMelech ties the geulah to it. One who lacks the longing must make a cheshbon hanefesh.

title.en: Using the remaining days; obstacles on the way

summary.en: The Rav urges the travelers to use the days left to prepare, as the Torah set preparation before Pesach, Shavuos, Sukkos and Shabbos. Meriting the land is not simple: Moshe Rabbeinu did not merit it, and Rabbi Zeira did not wait for a ferry. From the juxtaposition of Amalek to 'ki savo el ha'aretz' the Chareidim learns that whoever wishes to go meets obstacles, and must fight the yetzer hara and daven.

title.en: Reb Mendel Vitebsker and the yetzer hara

summary.en: The Rav tells how Reb Mendel Vitebsker, a great disciple of the Maggid, told the yetzer hara he had money for only one ticket, so it should stay behind; arriving by ship, he found it waiting, saying the one abroad had only been its messenger. The Rav explains that in Eretz Yisroel, the root of everything, the yetzer hara too is greater, so one must come ready for battle and pay the full price.

title.en: The Bas Ayin in Tzfas; diamonds on the ground

summary.en: After a word on 'eretz chemdah tovah' from bentching, the Rav tells of the Bas Ayin in Tzfas: in the great earthquake his chassidim crowded around him, and the half of his beis medrash where they stood did not collapse, as a plaque there still records. He then tells of a man who as a boy heard that the ground of Eretz Yisroel is covered with diamonds, came and saw none, was told he had not yet merited it, and after secluding himself in avodah rejoiced that he now saw them.

title.en: A diamond, not an acre

summary.en: The Rav contrasts an acre, which is small as land goes, with a diamond the size of an orange, which is enormous: Eretz Yisroel is small next to Russia, America or Egypt, but it is a huge diamond. Only one who believes, davens and toils feels it, as one feels Shabbos or the sweetness of a Gemara; learning in Eretz Yisroel is different, since its air makes one wise.

title.en: Knowing the halachos of the land; new four amos

summary.en: The Rav warns that one must know the mitzvos that depend on the land, terumos and maasros, orlah and shemitah, and be sure of what one eats, since it is easy to stumble. He tells how Reb Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld would vary his route to gain new four amos in Eretz Yisroel, since each step taken in holiness brings a new share in Torah.

title.en: Moshe Rabbeinu's praise before his last tefillah

summary.en: The Rav brings the Chasam Sofer's question: Moshe Rabbeinu spoke to Hashem face to face, as one familiar, so why only in his last tefillah to enter the land did he open with praise, as Chazal learn from him? He answers that in the land of Sichon and Og, which already had some of the kedusha of Eretz Yisroel, Moshe felt a holiness he had not felt even in heaven, and with it awe before Hashem. The end of this stretch is hard to follow in the recording.

title.en: Yerushalayim, the inner point

summary.en: The Rav returns to Eretz Yisroel as Shabbos and turns to Yerushalayim, the center and inner point of the land, above the portions of the tribes. The Mishnah lets one compel a spouse to move to Eretz Yisroel and from there to Yerushalayim, and Hashem's eyes and heart are there always; since the churban the gates of tefillah are closed, and great merits are needed to break through.

title.en: Tefillah in Eretz Yisroel: Reb Avraham Kalisker's letters

summary.en: The Rav brings the letters Reb Avraham Kalisker sent from Eretz Yisroel to his fellow disciples of the Maggid: at first the land seemed to hide itself, like a prospective kallah who does not show herself, and only later did they merit a tefillah such as they had never davened. The smallest tefillah in Eretz Yisroel is greater than the greatest elsewhere, and over the place of the Mikdash heaven is wide open.

title.en: The kedusha that remains; the Kosel HaMaaravi

summary.en: The Rav mentions the machlokes of the Rambam and Ramban on whether living in Eretz Yisroel is a mitzvah today, and the view that the first kedusha of Yerushalayim remains forever, as 'vahashimosi es mikdesheichem' shows. The Shechinah never left the Kosel HaMaaravi, many have been helped by davening there, and he tells how the Ohr HaChaim sent a poor talmid with a note to place between its stones.

title.en: The Kosel endures; prepare for the great Shabbos

summary.en: The Rav brings the Yismach Moshe that Shlomo HaMelech built knowing that the Kosel would remain after the churban, and that the survival of the Jewish people is bound to it. He closes: what earlier generations longed for in vain is now a plane ticket away, so the travelers should prepare with learning, davening and teshuvah, as before Rosh Hashana, for the great Shabbos of Eretz Yisroel, Yerushalayim and the kivrei tzaddikim.

catalogTitle: חשיבות הליכה לא"י - הכנה והתעוררות לפורים משולש בירושלים

oneLiner.en: Before a group journey to Yerushalayim for Purim Meshulash, the Rav explains that a journey to a holy place is itself a cleansing preparation, describes the holiness of Eretz Yisroel, Yerushalayim and Purim there, and gives practical guidance for traveling with seriousness, calm and derech eretz.

abstract.en: The Rav opens by noting that rabbanim speak about Purim before it, and announces that he will speak about Purim in Yerushalayim, since a journey is coming. A journey to a holy place or a holy person is a great tikkun hanefesh: Avraham was first told to go, the Jews passed through forty-two journeys, and the Ba'al Shem Tov's students traveled to their Rebbe. He warns of the trials of modern travel and stresses guarding the eyes. He then describes the unique holiness of Purim, the honor of Yerushalayim behind walled-city Purim, and Yerushalayim and Purim as places and times of unity. Drawing on 'eretz chemdah', he explains that the Avos and all generations longed for the land, and that a mitzvah there is greater and a sin worse. He closes with practical guidance: no pictures, calm visits, effort in avodah, kiddush Hashem, obeying organizers, and contentment for those who cannot go.

en: The Rav teaches that a journey to a holy place or to a tzaddik is itself a great tikkun hanefesh that prepares the vessels to receive the lights of the place.
Today's travel carries great trials, and guarding the eyes and thoughts on the way is itself part of the preparation for reaching the holy land, city and time.
Walled-city Purim was set from the time of Yehoshua bin Nun to give honor to Yerushalayim, so coming to Yerushalayim for Purim reaches the true intent of Shushan Purim.
Yerushalayim, the concentration of Eretz Yisroel, is the place of unity, and Purim is the time of unity, so Purim in Yerushalayim is the peak of achdus.
A healthy Jewish soul inherits from the Avos a desire for Eretz Yisroel, and all generations longed for it.
A mitzvah done in Eretz Yisroel, and especially in Yerushalayim, is far greater, and a sin there is far worse.
Whether one goes or stays is decreed in Heaven, and one who cannot go should be content with the mission Hashem gives him where he is.

title.en: A journey to holiness as tikkun hanefesh

summary.en: The Rav notes the custom of speaking about Purim before it and announces he will speak about Purim in Yerushalayim, as a journey is near. He explains that a journey to a holy place or person is a tikkun hanefesh, pointing to the command to Avraham to go and to the forty-two journeys in the desert.

title.en: The Rebbe Reb Elimelech and journeys to tzaddikim

summary.en: The Rav tells of a penitent sent to the Rebbe Reb Elimelech who was told on arrival that the journey had already rectified almost everything. He describes the journeys of the Ba'al Shem Tov's students to their Rebbe, likens them to the forty-two journeys and the days of sefirah, and explains that a journey repairs the vessels so they can receive the lights.

title.en: Old journeys to Meron and today's trials

summary.en: The Rav recalls how people traveled two weeks by donkey from Yerushalayim to Meron with great joy. He warns that today's travel, at airports and on planes, holds great trials, and that guarding the eyes and thoughts turns the journey into a greater preparation, since one sees Tziyon according to the eyes one brings.

title.en: The holiness of Purim and the honor of Yerushalayim

summary.en: The Rav describes the unique holiness of Purim, a new light greater even than Yom Kippur, and Purim as a time when prayer is accepted. He explains that walled-city Purim was set from the days of Yehoshua bin Nun to honor Yerushalayim, which lay in ruins at the time of the miracle, and connects this to Yerushalayim's future wall of fire.

title.en: Yerushalayim and Purim as unity

summary.en: The Rav says that a Jew traveling to Yerushalayim with longing arouses longing above for the rebuilding. Yerushalayim is the place of unity and Purim the time of unity, so traveling together with friends in unity prepares one to receive the lights; perhaps the small efforts of small people will bring the geulah.

title.en: Eretz chemdah: the longing of the Avos

summary.en: The Rav explains 'eretz chemdah' as the land the Avos desired, because their healthy desire sought only true good. A healthy Jew inherits this desire unless he has spoiled it; he brings Avraham, Moshe, Dovid, Amora'im who kissed the stones and rolled in the dust, and the Ramban's words on leaving home for Eretz Yisroel.

title.en: Mitzvos and sins weigh more in Eretz Yisroel

summary.en: The Rav explains that a mitzvah in a chosen time or place is multiplied, so a mitzvah in Eretz Yisroel and Yerushalayim is greater and a sin worse; a tzaddik there grows greater and a rasha worse. He speaks of prayers rising there through a thin barrier, the holiness of its fruits, Esav's merit of living in the land, and the merit the land brings in judgment.

title.en: Feeling the holy ground anew

summary.en: The Rav contrasts the mesirus nefesh needed to reach the land before the war with the open doors of today. He brings the Chasam Sofer that the ground of Eretz Yisroel is holier than the heavens of chutz la'aretz, warns that long familiarity dulls the feeling, and says the land should feel new every day, as the Chasam Sofer writes of one who truly understands its holiness.

title.en: Entering the land with awe and purity

summary.en: The Rav brings the Tanya's letter on awakening the old love and says a Jew should feel as if crossing the Yarden with Yehoshua. He brings Rav Hirsch on 'our feet stood' as the frozen awe of a pilgrim, speaks of Purim Meshulash thirty days before Pesach, and brings the Chareidim, from the Ramak, that the land is surrounded by water so one enters it in purity, seriously, as one enters Kol Nidrei.

title.en: No pictures, and visiting with menuchah

summary.en: The Rav warns that taking pictures removes the seriousness of great moments, as at a chuppah, which the Divrei Chaim compared to Rosh Hashanah, and asks that none be taken in Eretz Yisroel. He brings that 'menuchah' refers to Yerushalayim and urges visiting holy places calmly rather than rushing from grave to grave.

title.en: Working for the feeling, and kiddush Hashem

summary.en: Bringing the Ba'al Shem Tov's teaching on davening with a closed heart, the Rav says that at a holy place one does not feel, one should work with emunah, avodah before the gift of feeling. He urges preparing in the coming weeks with Torah, tefillah and sefarim, rejoicing with friends, and asks bochurim to make a kiddush Hashem on the plane by courtesy and helping others.

title.en: Discipline, derech eretz and those who stay

summary.en: The Rav asks the travelers to obey the organizers who work hard, since the trip's success depends on order, and to act with humility and derech eretz. He then turns to those who cannot go because of parents, livelihood or home circumstances, reminding them that Purim teaches nothing is chance and asking them not to cause anyone distress.

title.en: All is from Heaven; closing wishes

summary.en: The Rav explains that who goes and who stays is decreed in Heaven, recalling that the Ba'al Shem Tov, the Vilna Gaon and the Chofetz Chaim set out and had to turn back, and asks those who stay to be content with their mission. He closes with wishes to receive the lights of Purim wherever one is, and a short account of a gentile's letter to a Jew he sat beside on a flight.

catalogTitle: Emunah - The נסיון of the Last Generation

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that the test of the last generation before Mashiach is emunah, using the Chafetz Chaim's words after a dibbuk in Radin, and shows how in a time of hester panim the whole world becomes a test of faith.

abstract.en: The Rav recalls that the generations run in a cycle from Moshe Rabbeinu's generation to the generation before Mashiach, and that we now stand at its end. He explains what a dibbuk is and tells the story of a girl in Radin whose dibbuk Rabbi Elchonon Wasserman drove out as the Chafetz Chaim's messenger. The Chafetz Chaim then said there would be no more dibbukim until Mashiach, because a dibbuk makes emunah easy, and the test of this generation is emunah. The Rav explains why later dibbukim in Eretz Yisrael do not contradict this, and why open wonders of tzaddikim have become rare. Every generation has its own test: for the Noam Elimelech it was tzitzis, as seen in the Divrei Chaim's teshuvos on machine-made tzitzis. Today the Satan is given license in emunah; this is the hester panim the Torah foretold, and Adar and Purim are given to strengthen emunah.

en: The Chafetz Chaim said there would be no more dibbukim until Mashiach, because seeing a dibbuk makes emunah easy, while the test of this generation is emunah.
Every generation has its own test; in the time of the Noam Elimelech it was tzitzis, and today it is emunah.
Open wonders of tzaddikim, once common, have become rare like a flash of lightning in the dark, because Hashem's presence is now veiled.
Since the test of the time is emunah, the Satan has license to entice and trip people up in emunah, and everything a Jew meets today, even the radio and the media, is a test of faith.
This is the hester panim the Torah foretold for the period before Mashiach: Hashem is in every part of creation, but He is not seen.
The months of Adar and Purim were given to strengthen emunah, and the Rav urges holding on to emunah with all one's strength and setting time to learn and practice it.

Purim and the month of Adar

title.en: The cycle of generations and what a dibbuk is

summary.en: The Rav recalls that the generations run from Moshe Rabbeinu's generation to the one before Mashiach, when the cycle starts again, and that we are now at its end. He then explains what a dibbuk is: a very sinful soul, pursued by angels of destruction, that sometimes takes refuge in another person's body when it finds him doing a sin.

title.en: The dibbuk in Radin

summary.en: The Rav tells how a girl in Radin was tormented by a dibbuk, and the aged Chafetz Chaim sent his talmid Rabbi Elchonon Wasserman to drive it out. The dibbuk spoke about the townspeople, called the Chafetz Chaim a Tanna, said it entered her when she drank water without a brachah, asked that Mishnayos be learned for it, and left through her small toe.

title.en: Why there will be no more dibbukim

summary.en: The Rav brings the Chafetz Chaim's statement that there will be no more dibbukim until Mashiach, because a dibbuk makes emunah easy while the test of this generation is emunah. He explains that later dibbukim in Eretz Yisrael do not contradict this, since there Hashem's guidance is seen openly, and that open wonders of tzaddikim have become rare because of hester panim.

title.en: Tzitzis, the test of an earlier generation

summary.en: The Rav brings the Noam Elimelech that the test of his time was tzitzis, and the Divrei Chaim's teshuvos ruling machine-made tzitzis unfit because a machine cannot have intent lishmah; his son notes that the factory then burned down. In passing the Rav tells listeners to say l'shem kedushas tefillin when blackening tefillin, and that tzitzis a boy tied before bar mitzvah must be retied.

title.en: The Satan's license in the test of emunah

summary.en: The Rav explains that the Satan works to make people stumble in the test of each generation, bringing the Yaaros Devash on why people wear black on Shabbos. Since today's test is emunah, the whole world is one great test of faith: Jews mix with non-Jews, and the godless world enters the home through the media, so the Satan has a field day.

title.en: Hester panim before Mashiach, and holding on to emunah

summary.en: The Rav explains that in Nitzavim, Vayelech and Haazinu Moshe Rabbeinu boldly foretold the future, including the hester panim before Mashiach, when Hashem fills creation but is not seen. He says the months of Adar and Purim were given to strengthen emunah, and closes by urging listeners to hold on to emunah, learn about it and practice it, since it is the last test before Mashiach.

catalogTitle: י"ז תמוז - זמן לתקן הפגם של - "וימאסו בארץ חמדה". טעם להחלשת החיבה לא"י בזמננו והתעוררת לעוררה

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that the exile came from the sin of 'they despised the desirable land', that the days of Bein HaMetzarim are the time to repair it by reawakening the old love for Eretz Yisroel, and why that love has cooled in recent generations.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the daughters of Tzelofchad, whose love for the land earned them a parshah in the Torah, and with the passuk in Tehillim that the exile was decreed because Klal Yisroel 'despised the desirable land'. The repair, he says, is to cherish Eretz Yisroel as the Avos, Moshe Rabbeinu and the great tzaddikim did, and the Three Weeks are the time for it. He then explains why the longing has weakened: the Zionists took over the land, and the gedolim rightly feared sending people there. He goes on to the greatness of the land: the Torah was given for it, mitzvos and aveiros weigh more there, the unity of Klal Yisroel and the Yamim Tovim depend on it, and its holiness is felt on arrival but must be renewed every day. He ends by noting that the danger of the old Zionists has faded, so ehrliche Yidden may again cherish the land, and prays for the geulah.

en: According to the passuk in Tehillim, the exile among the nations came because of 'they despised the desirable land', and its repair is to cherish Eretz Yisroel.
The Avos, Moshe Rabbeinu and the tzaddikim of all generations longed for Eretz Yisroel, and the days of Bein HaMetzarim call for reawakening that old love.
In the last two generations the longing cooled, partly because the Zionists became the masters of the land and the gedolim feared that people who went there would be spoiled.
The Torah was given for Eretz Yisroel; a mitzvah there is far greater and an aveirah far more destructive than outside the land.
The unity of Klal Yisroel as a people, and with it the Yamim Tovim through the fixing of the months, exist only through Jews living in Eretz Yisroel.
The holiness of Eretz Yisroel is felt strongly on arrival, but a Jew there should feel it anew every day, as with Torah and mitzvos.
Today the danger that came from the old Zionists has faded, and ehrliche Yidden who learn Chumash and Rashi are the ones who still long for the land.

candidateTopics: Zionism and the weakening of longing for the land
Kiddush HaChodesh and the Yamim Tovim

title.en: The daughters of Tzelofchad and the despised land

summary.en: The Rav opens with the daughters of Tzelofchad, whose love of the land earned them a parshah, and with the inner greatness of the Three Weeks. He brings the passuk in Tehillim that the exile was decreed for 'they despised the desirable land', and says the repair is to value and rejoice in Eretz Yisroel.

title.en: The land of desire and the longing of the Avos

summary.en: The Rav brings Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer that Eretz Yisroel is to the lands what Shabbos is to the days, and describes the longing of the Avos and Moshe Rabbeinu's many tefillos to enter. He brings the Sifrei that dwelling in the land equals all the mitzvos and Rabbi Abba kissing the stones of Acco, and calls for reawakening the old love in these days.

title.en: The great ones who yearned for the land

summary.en: The Rav says our generation lacks the longing of earlier tzaddikim, and brings the Ramban, the Chasam Sofer and the Chofetz Chaim, who was held back by Heaven when he was already packed to go. He explains that great people were not let in because their tefillos there would have brought the geulah, and cites the Ramban's and the Vilna Gaon's words of longing.

title.en: Why the love cooled: the Zionists

summary.en: The Rav explains that in the last two generations the longing cooled because the Zionists became masters of the land and the gedolim feared people would be spoiled there, so ehrliche Yidden came to feel a resistance to it. He brings the Shomer Emunim and Rav Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld, who says the meraglim foresaw by ruach hakodesh the falling generations in the land.

title.en: Greater holiness, greater danger

summary.en: The Rav explains that the yetzer hara in Eretz Yisroel is greater, so the land is not for everyone, and a mitzvah or an aveirah there weighs far more. The reason is that the Torah was given for the land, which is why the Avos kept the mitzvos only there, and why the dor hamidbar should have gone in with simple trust.

title.en: Unity of the people and the Yamim Tovim

summary.en: The Rav brings the Sefer Chareidim that one must long for the land, and explains that Jews are one people only through Eretz Yisroel, as seen from the halachah of the 'kahal'. From the Rambam he shows that the months, and so the Yamim Tovim that give a Jew his life of emunah all year, can be fixed only through Jews in Eretz Yisroel.

title.en: Mitzvos in exile as signposts

summary.en: The Rav brings Rashi on 'and you shall place these words' that mitzvos are kept in exile as signposts, so that they will not be new when the Jews return. He then explains that a mitzvah or a blatt Gemara in Eretz Yisroel is worth far more than outside, as Shabbos is to the weekdays, and an aveirah there causes far greater destruction.

title.en: Torah of Eretz Yisroel and the end of idolatry

summary.en: The Rav brings the Midrash that there is no Torah like the Torah of Eretz Yisroel, and says one sees it in the success of those who learn there and the sefarim written there; Yerushalayim is holier still, and one must be careful there. He then explains that the yetzer hara for avodah zarah was nullified only by those who had the merit of the land, Yehoshua and the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah, not by Moshe Rabbeinu.

title.en: A day in Your courts, and fresh holiness

summary.en: The Rav brings 'better one day in Your courts than a thousand' and Rashi's reading of it as a thousand years, and the teaching that living in the land brings a neshamah of holiness. He describes the feeling on arriving, like accepting Shabbos, Rav Chaim Shmuelevitz's experience, and says the feeling fades with habit though every mitzvah should be as new as the day it was given.

title.en: Tefillin, the fruits and the lasting holiness

summary.en: The Rav says a Jew in Eretz Yisroel should feel each day as if he just arrived, and that this freshness is written in the parshiyos of tefillin, which hold the foundations of Yiddishkeit. He speaks of the joy of a brachah on the fruits of the land, and brings the Rambam that the holiness of the Shechinah in the land never ceases, and the Sefer Chareidim that one must honor the land.

title.en: The Zionists then and now, and a closing tefillah

summary.en: The Rav contrasts the old settlers' mesiras nefesh and the old Zionists' remaining longing with today's leaders, for whom the land means nothing, without entering the political question. Only ehrliche Yidden who learn Chumash and Rashi still long for it, and he brings the Chasam Sofer that speaking of the land brings yiras shamayim. He closes by tying it to the Three Weeks and parshas Pinchas and prays for the geulah.

catalogTitle: צד א: בביהכ"נ האוה"ח הק' - צריכים לעורר חיבה ישנה אל ארץ הקודש. צד ב: קבר רחל - ביי קבר רחל קען מען אלעס אויספויעלן

oneLiner.en: Speaking in Jerusalem and then at Kever Rachel, the Rav explains how a Jew must rekindle the ancient love for Eretz Yisroel as if it were given to him today, and why at the grave of Rachel, the mother of Klal Yisroel, one can accomplish everything.

abstract.en: The Rav opens in Jerusalem with the Ba'al HaTanya's call to awaken the ancient love of the Holy Land, a love that must burn like fire, as Rashi says of the gift of the land: as if given today. He traces this longing from the Avos through the Ramban, the Vilna Gaon and the Chofetz Chaim. He explains that only in Eretz Yisroel are Jews a single nation, that it is the gate of heaven where tefillos pass unblocked, and that Jerusalem must never become routine; one must prepare before coming to the Kosel. On the second side, at Kever Rachel, he explains that Rachel weeps for her children throughout the galus, connects Beis Lechem with Yovel and the fifty days to Rosh Hashanah, and brings the Midrash in which Rachel's plea was answered because she overcame jealousy, beginning the repair of the diminished moon.

en: The Rav says the love of Eretz Yisroel must be awakened like a burning fire, as though Hashem gave the land today, and at the very least with some warmth.
Jews have always longed for Eretz Yisroel with self-sacrifice, from the Avos and Moshe Rabbeinu through the Amora'im, the Ramban and the great tzaddikim of later generations.
Eretz Yisroel is the gate of heaven: the clouds that block tefillos are thin there and absent over Har HaBayis, so one must come to Jerusalem and the Kosel prepared and with freshness.
Rachel weeps for her children not only at the churban but throughout the galus, and she is the mother of Klal Yisroel.
At Kever Rachel one can accomplish everything, as by a mother, and it is a fitting place to daven for Klal Yisroel.
Rachel's plea was accepted where the Avos and Imahos were not, because she overcame jealousy and gave over the signs to her sister.

title.en: Awakening the ancient love of the Holy Land

summary.en: Sitting in Jerusalem facing Har HaBayis, the Rav takes the opportunity to speak about Eretz Yisroel. He brings the Ba'al HaTanya's words about awakening the ancient love of the Holy Land and Rashi's teaching that the land should be seen as given today, so that the love burns like fire, or at least with some warmth.

title.en: The longing of the generations for the land

summary.en: The Rav shows the longing for Eretz Yisroel through the generations: the Avos, Moshe Rabbeinu's plea, the Amora'im who kissed its stones, the Ramban's words, and the Vilna Gaon and Chofetz Chaim, whom Heaven held back. He brings the Yalkut that Hashem found no land fit for Israel except Eretz Yisroel.

title.en: A single nation in the land; the gate of heaven

summary.en: The Rav explains from the Sefer Chareidim and the passuk 'goy echad ba'aretz' that only in Eretz Yisroel are Jews one nation, comparing a Jew in chutz la'aretz to an animal in a zoo. He calls the land the gate of heaven, brings the Arizal's constant ruach hakodesh there and the Midrash on 'bezos' as the merit of Jerusalem, and warns that coming to Jerusalem must not become routine.

title.en: Preparing for the Kosel; seeing with the heart

summary.en: The Rav tells of a Rebbe who would not pass the Kosel without preparation, and explains that the clouds blocking tefillos are absent over Har HaBayis. He brings Rav Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld's words that his only merit was dwelling in the holy city, and closes with the vision of the third Beis HaMikdash on Shabbos Chazon, seen with the heart.

title.en: Gap in the recording; Shabbos niggunim

summary.en: Long stretches with almost no transcribed speech at the end of the first side and the start of the second, with a brief mention of singing Shabbos niggunim.

title.en: Rachel weeps for her children; Beis Lechem and Yovel

summary.en: At Kever Rachel the Rav explains that Rachel weeps for her children throughout the galus, as the mother of Klal Yisroel. He says each part of Eretz Yisroel corresponds to a part of the Torah, and Beis Lechem corresponds to Yovel, the return of each man to his inheritance, which he links to 'veshavu vanim ligvulam' and to the fiftieth day of Matan Torah.

title.en: Fifty days to Rosh Hashanah; Rachel and Moshiach

summary.en: The Rav counts fifty days from after Tisha B'Av to Rosh Hashanah, the day of the shofar like Yovel, and says this is an auspicious time to daven at Kever Rachel, where one can accomplish everything as by a mother. He speaks of Moshiach being revealed nearby at Migdal Eder, of Rachel as the aspect of the Shechinah and of Shabbos, and of tzaddikim who gathered there on Friday to sing Shabbos niggunim. A long stretch of apparent singing follows.

title.en: Rachel's plea and the repair of the moon

summary.en: The Rav brings the Midrash cited by Rashi: when Menashe placed an idol in the Heichal, the Avos and Imahos could not appease Hashem, but Rachel pleaded that she had overcome her jealousy and given her sister the signs, and she was answered. He explains that Rachel is the aspect of the moon, whose jealousy brought its diminishing, the source of the jealousy and hatred that brought galus, and that Rachel began its repair.

title.en: Long gap; a brief closing fragment

summary.en: A very long stretch with almost no transcribed speech, followed by a short unrelated fragment about the prophet Yeshayahu coming to console.

catalogTitle: נצבים וילך - The Prophecy of this Century

oneLiner.en: The Rav shows that Nitzavim-Vayelech, the sedra of the present century according to the Gra, foretells both the hester panim and destruction of this era and the teshuvah and redemption that follow, with the healing placed before the blow.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the end of the galus as a time of hester panim, in which even the concealment is concealed. He brings the teaching of the Vilna Gaon, recorded by his talmidim, that the sedras of Devarim correspond to the centuries of the sixth millennium, and the Gra's answer to Reb Chaim of Volozhin that he himself is the 'even shleimah' of Ki Seitzei. Since Nitzavim and Vayelech count as one sedra, they hold the events of the century that began in 5700. He tells how, as a boy in 1939, he saw the shul weep on Rosh Hashanah while the boys trusted the radio that Germany would fall in days. Vayelech foretells the hester panim; Nitzavim foretells the teshuvah and ingathering. Nitzavim comes first because Hashem prepares the refuah before the makah, and they are two sedras because galus and geulah are two different programs. He closes with today's hester panim and a call to teshuvah.

en: According to the Gra, each sedra of Devarim corresponds to a century of the sixth millennium, and the Gra found himself in Ki Seitzei in the words 'even shleimah', Eliyahu ben Shlomo.
Nitzavim and Vayelech count as one sedra, as the Masorah shows and as answers the Zohar's count of 53 sedras, so they are the sedra of the present century.
Vayelech foretells the hester panim and the tragedy of the Tav-Shin years, and Nitzavim foretells the teshuvah, the ingathering and the return to Eretz Yisrael.
Nitzavim's consolation comes before Vayelech's suffering because with the Jewish people Hashem prepares the refuah before the makah, as a surgeon does.
Galus and geulah fall in one century but cannot share one sedra, because a sedra is a 'program' and the world after Mashiach will run on an entirely new order.
The Rav describes the present as hester panim, with rising antisemitism and 'Haman becoming powerful', and says Hashem wants to arouse the Jewish people to teshuvah.

title.en: Each sedra of Devarim is a century

summary.en: The Rav describes the end of the galus as hester panim and brings the Gra's teaching that the ten sedras of Devarim match the centuries of the sixth millennium, with the Gra's answer to Reb Chaim of Volozhin. He shows that Nitzavim-Vayelech count as one sedra, which places our century in it.

title.en: Rosh Hashanah 1939 in Williamsburg

summary.en: The Rav tells how, as a boy in Torah Vodaath before the war, a classmate's radio report convinced the boys that Germany would be crushed in days, and how on Rosh Hashanah he saw the whole shul weeping for relatives in Poland. The war lasted five years and a third of Klal Yisrael was killed.

title.en: Vayelech's hester panim, Nitzavim's teshuvah

summary.en: The Rav goes through Vayelech, where Moshe Rabbeinu foretells that Hashem will hide His face and has it written down as testimony, and then Nitzavim, which foretells teshuvah in galus, the ingathering and the return to Eretz Yisrael. He points to the baalei teshuvah of today as the start of that prophecy.

title.en: The refuah before the makah

summary.en: The Rav asks why the consolation of Nitzavim comes before the suffering of Vayelech, and why one sedra is split in two. He answers the first from the Gemara that Hashem prepares the refuah before the makah for the Jewish people, as in the Megillah, and explains it with the difference between a murderer and a surgeon.

title.en: A sedra is a program

summary.en: The Rav explains that a sedra is a 'program' that tells what is happening, and tells how the Maggid of Mezritch chose the future Ba'al HaTanya as his baal korei. Since the world after Mashiach will run on a new order, galus and geulah cannot be in one sedra.

title.en: Today's hester panim and the call to teshuvah

summary.en: The Rav brings the Gemara that the story of Esther is alluded to in the Torah's hester panim and compares the Jews' fall in the days of Achashverosh to today. He points to rising antisemitism in Austria and America and closes that Hashem wants to stir the Jewish people to teshuvah, with a wish for the consolations of this century.

catalogTitle: צד א: מערת המכפלה - שורש האמונה. כותל המערבי - גודל כח התפילה שם צד ב: בחצר שנולד שם הארי' הק' - מקום התגלות אור הגנוז

oneLiner.en: Speaking at the holy places of Eretz Yisroel, the Rav explains what each place holds: Kever Rachel the softer judgment of the second day of Rosh Hashanah, Ramah the tefillah of Chana, the Me'aras HaMachpela the root of emunah, the Kosel the gate of tefillah, and the Arizal's birthplace the revelation of the hidden light.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with a Midrash: whether the vineyard's wine is good or bad, it belongs to the King, and so the Jewish people remain Hashem's even when they sin; Yeshayahu's 'Nachamu' comforts all generations. At Kever Rachel he explains that Leah is the harsh judgment of the first day of Rosh Hashanah and Rachel the softer judgment of the second; what exists in time exists in place, so here one davens for a good judgment. At Ramah he speaks of Chana, the soul of Rosh Hashanah, and of Shmuel's gilgulim. At the Me'aras HaMachpela, the cradle of emunah, he urges davening like Kalev to be saved from today's 'counsel of the spies', and rejoicing like the Ramban. He calls the Kosel the main post office of tefillah, and at the Arizal's birthplace speaks of the hidden light and a new start in serving Hashem.

en: Like the wine of the King's vineyard, the Jewish people belong to Hashem whether they are good or bad, and this is a chizuk for every Jew who wonders what connection he still has with Hashem.
Kever Rachel is the place of the second day of Rosh Hashanah, the softer judgment, so it is a place to daven for a good judgment for all Jews.
Chana, whose tefillah the Gemara learns many laws of prayer from and whose story is read on Rosh Hashanah, is the soul of Rosh Hashanah, and she rests with Shmuel at Ramah.
The Me'aras HaMachpela, resting place of the Avos, is the root and cradle of emunah, and there one should daven, as Kalev did, to be saved from the 'counsel of the spies' of one's own generation.
The Rav says one should rejoice and make a yom tov over having merited to come to the Me'aras HaMachpela and the Kosel, and use every moment there.
The Kosel is the 'main post office' from which tefillos go up, so the time there should not be wasted.
At the place where the Arizal, a revelation of the hidden light, was born, each person can have a new point of longing and of doing Hashem's will born within him.

summary.en: The Rav brings the Midrash of the King whose vineyard's wine, good or bad, is always his, applies it to Hashem calling the Jews 'My people', and draws chizuk from it. He then brings the Midrash that Yeshayahu's 'Nachamu nachamu ami' comforts all generations.

summary.en: A long stretch of over three minutes with only a few garbled words transcribed.

title.en: Kever Rachel and the second day of Rosh Hashanah

summary.en: At Kever Rachel the Rav explains that Leah is the harsh judgment of the first day of Rosh Hashanah and Rachel the softer judgment of the second, when Hashem hears Rachel's weeping. Since what exists in time exists in place, this is the place of the second day, and here one can daven for a good judgment.

title.en: Untranscribed stretch at Kever Rachel

summary.en: About nine and a half minutes with almost nothing transcribed, apparently singing or davening at the kever.

title.en: The haftoros of Rachel and Chana

summary.en: The Rav says the haftorah of the second day of Rosh Hashanah speaks of Rachel and holds more comfort than all of Yeshayahu. At Ramah he calls Chana the soul of Rosh Hashanah and explains Shmuel's gilgulim as Korach and Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah, which answers 'like seventy years' and Rabbi Elazar's need for wealth; Shmuel was the first navi and Chana the first to call Hashem Tzevakos.

title.en: Me'aras HaMachpela, cradle of emunah

summary.en: The Rav explains that, like Kalev who went to Chevron to be saved from the spies, one comes to the Avos, the root of emunah, to be saved from today's 'counsel of the spies': kefirah, pritzus and electronic devices. He brings the Zohar on Yaakov's greatness and the Ramban, who made a yearly yom tov for having davened at the Mikdash and the Machpela.

title.en: The merit of Chevron and the dancing mountains

summary.en: The Rav brings the announcement in the Beis Hamikdash that the east was lit 'until Chevron', to recall the merit of the Avos, tells how the Lelover took the Shinever Rav to Chevron and showed him the mountains dancing, and says the light of Gan Eden that Adam Harishon saw here is why Avraham wanted this cave. He urges using the place to daven for emunah, yiras Shamayim and yeshuos.

title.en: The Kosel, main post office of tefillah

summary.en: The Rav tells of a Jew who toured the holy places each year and, on reaching Yerushalayim, ran to the Kosel calling it the main post office. He says that though one must sit and learn all year, this time should be used to daven there, and a few words of Selichos are sung.

title.en: The Arizal's birthplace and the hidden light

summary.en: At the place where the Arizal was born, the Rav speaks of the sod in every Jew that only Hashem sees, of the Arizal's bond with Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and the month of Av, and of the soul of the hidden light that came down through Rashbi, the Arizal and the Ba'al Shem Tov. He closes that here each person can begin anew in serving Hashem, with a tefillah for the geulah.

catalogTitle: צד א: קבר רחל - מהר"ל - בזכות רחל אמנו ישובו ישראל מגלותם. צד ב: קבר שמאול הנביא - מקום להתפלל על פקודת עקרות ברוחניות ועל הרמת קרן משיח

oneLiner.en: Through the Maharal, the Rav explains that Rachel, the akeres habayis who gathers Klal Yisrael, was buried on the road so that her power to gather goes with the Jews into exile, and he presents the kever of Shmuel and Chana as a place to pray for those who are spiritually barren and for the raising of the horn of Moshiach.

abstract.en: The Rav learns the Maharal on the Midrash that Yaakov buried Rachel on the road to Efras so she would ask mercy for her children in exile. A wife is called 'bayis' because the home gathers the scattered family, and Rachel was Yaakov's akeres habayis. The road scatters; since exile is a road, Rachel's gathering power goes with the Jews, and in her merit they return. He links this to Beis Lechem, the place of Moshiach. After a long unrecorded stretch he presents Sefer Devarim as the seventh book, the kallah, like Shabbos. At the kever of Shmuel and Chana he ties them to Rosh Hashanah, brings the Arizal on Shmuel's gilgulim, and calls the place a site to pray for the barren, for fruitful Torah and tefilah, and for Moshiach's horn. He closes on punctual Shabbos davening.

en: A wife is called 'bayis' because a home gathers and unites the scattered family, and Rachel was the akeres habayis of Yaakov.
Rachel was buried on the road, the opposite of a home, so that her gathering power would accompany the Jews on the road of exile.
In the merit of Rachel's gathering power the Jews will return from their exile, and her place near Beis Lechem is the place of Moshiach.
Shmuel and Chana are bound up with Rosh Hashanah: Chana's story is its haftorah and the laws of tefilah are learned from her.
The kever of Shmuel and Chana is a place to pray for the barren to be remembered, and also that one's Torah and tefilah not be 'barren' without fruit.
Shmuel brought kingship into the world, anointing Shaul from Rachel and David from Leah, so his place is fitting to pray for the raising of Moshiach's horn.
Shacharis is the main tefilah and sets the whole day, and the Shabbos morning davening sets the whole Shabbos, so one must come on time.

title.en: The Maharal: Rachel as akeres habayis

summary.en: The Rav opens the Maharal on the Midrash about why Yaakov buried Rachel on the road to Efras, with the pesukim of Rachel weeping for her children. He explains that a wife is called 'bayis' because a home gathers the scattered family, and Rachel was Yaakov's akeres habayis.

title.en: Buried on the road, gathering the exiles

summary.en: The Rav explains that the road is the opposite of a home, and Rachel was buried there so her gathering power goes with the Jews into exile; in her merit they return. He ties this to Shabbos Chazon and to Beis Lechem, the place of Moshiach, and speaks of praying at her kever.

title.en: Sefer Devarim, the seventh book and the kallah

summary.en: The Rav counts Sefer Devarim as the seventh book, like Shabbos the seventh day, and calls both the kallah. Devarim begins on Shabbos Chazon, and he brings the passuk that Hashem does not despise Klal Yisrael in their enemies' land, for they are His kallah.

summary.en: A single flagged segment of about six minutes with only a few garbled words; the audio here was not transcribed.

title.en: Shmuel, Chana and Rosh Hashanah

summary.en: After wishing for Shabbosos with proper davening, the Rav turns to the kever of Shmuel and Chana and ties both to Rosh Hashanah. He brings the Arizal that Shmuel was a gilgul from Korach and later came back as Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah, and the Gemara that Shmuel never took benefit from others.

title.en: Praying for the barren and for Moshiach's horn

summary.en: The Rav brings that Chana first called Hashem 'Tzevakos' and was one of the seven barren women, so her kever is a place for the barren to be remembered, and also to pray that one's Torah and tefilah not be barren. Since Shmuel anointed Shaul and David and Chana's song ends with the raising of Moshiach's horn, it is a place to pray for that too.

title.en: Coming on time to Shabbos Shacharis

summary.en: Pointing to the parsha of yirah in the week's sidra, the Rav stresses coming on time to Shabbos morning davening: Shacharis sets the whole day and the whole Shabbos, the Arizal speaks of a stronger neshamah yeseirah on Shabbos morning, and the Shabbos mizmorim, brachos and Nishmas are entirely different from the weekday ones.

title.en: A story and the holiness of the beis medrash

summary.en: The Rav tells a story involving poritzim and a lavish meal, whose details the transcript mostly loses. He then speaks of the great kindness of having a holy beis medrash where great tzaddikim davened.

title.en: Davening in a holy place; Kedushah and the tish

summary.en: The Rav says that a place where tzaddikim davened is a help to daven better, calls the Shabbos Kedushah of Keser the highest of the week, and says a Friday-night tish is a great thing but must not come at the expense of davening. He returns to Chana as the source of the laws of tefilah and closes asking for yiras shamayim.

catalogTitle: דברי התעוררות והדרכה להנוסעים לא"י לפורים משולש

oneLiner.en: Before a group journey to Eretz Yisroel for a Purim that falls on Shabbos, the Rav explains the holiness of the land and of Purim in Yerushalayim, and guides the travelers on how to prepare, how to feel, and how to behave on the way and on Purim.

abstract.en: The Rav opens by calling Eretz Yisroel the 'eretz chemdah', the desired land, as Shabbos is the most desired of days, and contrasts the mesiras nefesh of earlier generations with today's easy travel. Hashem's eyes are always on the land, so living there or even visiting demands a cheshbon: holiness magnifies both merit and damage, as on Shabbos. He describes the Shabbos Purim of Yerushalayim, which only exists there, and through the Arizal explains why it spreads over three days. Tefillos are accepted in Eretz Yisroel, as shown from Yehoshua and Yaakov's fear of Esav. Through the Chasam Sofer he teaches that the land must be seen with different eyes, and shows that one day of Purim makes a person a resident of Yerushalayim. He warns not to be broken if the feeling does not come, with stories of tzaddikim, and closes with guidance on kiddush Hashem during the flight and a serious Purim without drunkenness.

en: Earlier generations reached Eretz Yisroel only with great mesiras nefesh, and great tzaddikim were held back from Heaven; today a large part of Klal Yisroel lives there and even a visit is not a waste of time.
Because Hashem's special providence rests on Eretz Yisroel, being there demands worthiness, and a traveler must make a cheshbon of why he is going.
The Purim that falls on Shabbos in Yerushalayim exists only there, and its power is so great that it spreads over three days.
Eretz Yisroel is the place where tefillos are accepted, which is why tzaddikim abroad would write there asking to be davened for.
One day of Purim in Yerushalayim makes a person a resident of the city with all its laws, although residency in Eretz Yisroel normally takes thirty days.
If one feels no special warmth in Eretz Yisroel he should not be broken: the feeling is a gift from Heaven, and sometimes Hashem asks for avodah without it.
On the way and on Purim the travelers must make a kiddush Hashem: quiet, courteous behavior on the airplane and a Purim with serious moments, not drunkenness.

title.en: The desired land and the mesiras nefesh of old

summary.en: The Rav says he will review known matters before the trip. He explains 'eretz chemdah', the land the Avos desired, as Shabbos is the most desired of days, recalls Moshe Rabbeinu's many tefillos to enter and Dovid's love for its very stones, and contrasts today's comfortable flight with the dangerous journeys of earlier generations and the Ramban, who left family and students to come.

title.en: Held back then, let in now

summary.en: The Rav tells how the Gra had to turn back midway and how the Chofetz Chaim's packed bags stayed home when his rebbetzin fell ill, while today a third of Klal Yisroel lives in the land and a visit is no waste of time. From the passuk that Hashem's eyes are on the land all year he explains its special providence, and says that living there is a serious undertaking that requires being worthy.

title.en: Entering a holy place with preparation

summary.en: The Rav explains that Yerushalayim was meant for coming three times a year to strengthen one's yiras Shamayim, and that one must prepare for Eretz Yisroel as for entering a beis medrash, since a street there is holier than a shul abroad. He tells that the Chasam Sofer did not go but urged his talmidim to, and brings his words that the land makes a tzaddik greater, while its wicked become worse.

title.en: Greater holiness, greater responsibility

summary.en: Comparing the land to Shabbos, when a blatt Gemara is holier and a sin graver, the Rav explains that in Eretz Yisroel one receives a different neshamah, brings the Gemara's levels of four amos, thirty days and a full year, and compares a careless visitor to one entering the king's court in sackcloth. Therefore one must make a cheshbon before going and not travel merely for sightseeing.

title.en: Shabbos Purim in Yerushalayim

summary.en: The Rav describes a Shabbos and Nishmas in Eretz Yisroel and the Purim that falls on Shabbos, which can only be kept in Yerushalayim. Through the Arizal's explanation of why chutz la'aretz needs two days of Yom Tov, he shows why this Purim spreads over three days, and then explains that Eretz Yisroel is the place where tefillos are accepted.

title.en: The zechus of Eretz Yisroel

summary.en: The Rav brings the Gemara that Yehoshua was punished for not davening away the yetzer hara of avodah zarah, and explains why Moshe Rabbeinu could not do it while Yehoshua could: he was in Eretz Yisroel. He adds the Ramak's teaching that the land is surrounded by water on four sides, and Chazal's explanation that Yaakov feared Esav because of his kibbud av and the zechus of living in the land.

title.en: Decrees undone and the signs of desire

summary.en: The Rav brings the Gemara that one sentenced abroad who flees to Eretz Yisroel is judged again, since a merit may be found for him there, and Avraham Avinu's years in the land, to show that decrees can be undone there. He cites the Sefer Chareidim on longing for the land, gives two signs of spiritual sickness, lacking desire to learn and to go to Eretz Yisroel, and tells the travelers to examine whether they long for the trip or for its holiness.

title.en: Seeing the land with different eyes

summary.en: The Rav brings the Chasam Sofer that the earth of Eretz Yisroel is holier than the heavens of chutz la'aretz, and compares looking at the land to looking at a Jew and a goy: the same outward form, an entirely different thing. He mentions Dovid HaMelech's pride that his feet stood in Yerushalayim, and quotes the Chasam Sofer in Parshas Shelach that one who understands the holiness of the land and of his soul would give everything just to see it.

title.en: One day of Purim makes a citizen

summary.en: The Rav cautions against going into debt for the trip, then recalls the three levels of settling the land and that residency normally requires thirty days. On Purim, however, one day in Yerushalayim makes a person a resident of a walled city with all its laws, just as being in the land for the seven days of Sukkos suffices because dwelling in a sukkah for seven days counts as dwelling.

title.en: The Kosel, the prophets and the Shabbos of Purim

summary.en: The Rav brings the Maharal and Sfas Emes that Purim in Yerushalayim is far greater, and the Arvei Nachal that in galus all the holiness of the Beis Hamikdash is concentrated in the Kosel. From the Gemara that every place grows its own plants he shows that Yerushalayim grows nevi'im, explains that the power of Purim spreads beyond the old city, and teaches that Mordechai and Esther originally instituted reading the Megillah on Shabbos, so the whole power of this Purim rests in its Shabbos.

title.en: When the feeling does not come

summary.en: The Rav tells the travelers to prepare in the weeks before the trip by learning with more diligence and davening better, and not to be shaken if in Eretz Yisroel they feel a blocked heart. He explains that a sweet feeling in Torah and tefillah is 'avodas matanah', a gift from Heaven, brings the Ohr HaChaim on how intense the true pleasure of Torah is, and says that sometimes Hashem asks for labor without the gift.

title.en: Two tefillos that felt dry

summary.en: The Rav tells of R' Avraham Kalisker's letters from Eretz Yisroel, where he concluded that his first, dry tefillah there was greater than a famous minchah under a tree, and of R' Sholom of Prohobisht, whose strained Erev Rosh Hashanah minchah brought tikkun to thousands of souls, as R' Nachum of Chernobyl told him. He concludes that one should ask for a feeling in the land but not be disappointed without it.

title.en: Kiddush Hashem on the airplane

summary.en: The Rav asks the bachurim and yungeleit to make a kiddush Hashem on the flight: no shouting, no trouble for the crew, and saying thank you, as he illustrates from the custom in Oberland of kissing one's mother's hand after a meal. He reports that rabbanim now say not to block the aisles with minyanim but to daven seated, distinguishes between halachah and a chumra that must be weighed, and urges helping others with their baggage.

title.en: A serious Purim and a tefillah for the journey

summary.en: The Rav warns against wild behavior and drunkenness on Purim, distinguishing the Satmar Rav's holy intoxication from ordinary people, and brings the Rambam, the Meiri and the Mishnah Berurah on drinking a little and going to sleep. He recalls R' Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz insisting on a serious moment at the Purim seudah, brings R' Zeira who crossed the Yarden on a rope bridge lest he lose the chance, and ends with a tefillah that the journey succeed.

catalogTitle: Purim - Hashem Behind the Cloak of עשו

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that the miracles of Purim and Adar are real but hidden, cloaked by the concealment of Amalek, and that the Megillah trains a Jew to find Hashem's name behind the cloak of nature.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the greatness of Purim: the Arizal places it above every Yom Tov, and the Chasam Sofer says the kedushah of the Megillah exceeds that of the anointing oil. Adar is the heel of the year, farthest from Nissan, and it matches the lowest souls of Klal Yisrael, the ones Amalek attacked when the clouds of glory rejected them. Every Jew still keeps a hidden point of love for Hashem, and so the Purim miracle came even for sinners; at the very feast they wrongly enjoyed, Hashem removed Vashti to make room for Esther. Nissan holds revealed miracles, Adar hidden ones, as the Bnei Yissaschar's parable of the dying patient shows. The Megillah has no open miracle and no name of Hashem because Amalek conceals Him, yet His name is hidden at its turning points. The Megillah teaches a Jew to read Hashem's plan in world events and in his own life.

en: Adar, the last month and farthest from Nissan, corresponds to the lowest souls of Klal Yisrael, and the Purim miracle was given even for those who had sinned.
Every Jew, even a great rasha, has a hidden point inherited from the Avos where he wants to be good, and so Hashem's love for him remains.
Nissan is the month of revealed miracles, while the miracles of Adar are hidden, cloaked in nature.
The Megillah shows no open miracle and does not mention Hashem's name because Amalek's concealment hides Hashem.
The Megillah is an exercise in finding Hashem's name hidden in whatever happens in the world and in one's own life.

title.en: Purim, the heel of the year, and Hashem's love

summary.en: The Rav describes the greatness of Purim, citing the Arizal and the Chasam Sofer, and explains that Adar, the heel of the year, matches the lowest souls whom Amalek attacked. Since every Jew keeps a hidden love for Hashem, the Purim miracle came even for sinners, prepared at the very feast of Achashverosh, like a father's mercy described in Parshas Ki Sisa.

title.en: Revealed miracles and hidden miracles

summary.en: The Rav contrasts Nissan, the month of open miracles, with Adar, where the Megillah reads like a story without miracles and without Hashem's name. He brings the Bnei Yissaschar's parable of a dying patient whose distant doctor and medicine arrive just in time, showing Hashem's hidden hand.

title.en: Every step of the Megillah is part of the miracle

summary.en: The Rav shows how each event in the Megillah happens just in time and fits a plan, and says a person who examines his own day would see miracles in it too. Adar is named for the aderes, a cloak: its miracles are cloaked in nature. He then asks why the Megillah shows no miracles.

title.en: Amalek hides Hashem's name

summary.en: The Rav answers that Amalek conceals Hashem, as Rashi explains that Hashem's name and throne are incomplete because of Amalek. In the Megillah Hashem is hidden in the word HaMelech, which, like kes Kah and Haman, equals 95; Achashverosh is a puppet on Hashem's strings, and Hashem's name is hidden at the Megillah's turning points.

title.en: Learning to read the hidden plan

summary.en: The Rav concludes that the Megillah is an exercise in finding Hashem's name in everything that happens, like a trained doctor reading an X-ray or a reader seeing a master plan in the newspaper. Like a masked Purim visitor, the world is only a shroud with Hashem underneath, and a person who looks into the events of his life will see miracles.

catalogTitle: שמשון הגיבור - הוא נוקם כנגד הפאליסטינער בגלל יהודים שבעיקבתא דמשיחא (יארצייט של סקולענר רבי זצ”ל) שמעון הצדיק - שיריים של אנשי כנה"ג. קבר רחל - ווי לאנג וועט זי וויינען!?

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that Shimshon's strength lay in his hair, which stands for the lowest, cut-off Jews of the generation before Moshiach, and that Shimshon's prayer and his war against the Plishtim continue in that generation.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the teaching that Yaakov, blessing Dan, saw Shimshon and thought he was Moshiach, then saw him fall and said 'lishuascha kivisi Hashem'. Chazal seem to contradict themselves about Shimshon; the Rav explains that Shimshon went down to assimilating Jews to pull them out, with intent for Heaven. His strength was in his hair, the lowest parts of Klal Yisroel, Dan being the last tribe. The nazir's hair is a crown, 'nezer Elokav al rosho', the gematria of ikvesa d'meshicha: the last Jews will become the crown. He connects Shimshon's war against the Plishtim, his prayer 'zochreini na' and his destruction of Aza to the Palestinians of today, and calls on the listeners to daven with Shimshon. After prayer and a niggun, he speaks briefly about Shimon HaTzaddik.

en: Shimshon went down to the lowest levels, to assimilating Jews, in order to pull them out, and his intent was for the sake of Heaven.
Shimshon's strength was in his hair, which stands for the lowest Jews who are cut off from Klal Yisroel, the Jews of ikvesa d'meshicha.
The lowest and last Jews, the generation before Moshiach, will become the crown of Klal Yisroel and the greatest tzaddikim.
The Palestinians take their name from the Plishtim, and a name defines a thing, so Shimshon's war against the Plishtim continues against them.
Yaakov's prayer 'lishuascha kivisi Hashem' was for the generation of ikvesa d'meshicha, that through their tefillos they should hold out through the last moments of the exile.
Shimon HaTzaddik, one of the remnants of the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah, is the first named in the chain of the Oral Torah after Moshe and led the Jews into the era of the Tanna'im.

summary.en: The Rav explains that the cut-off hair stands for the lost Jews of the generation before Moshiach, whom Hashem's tzaddikim raise up. The nazir's hair is a crown, and 'nezer Elokav al rosho' is the gematria of ikvesa d'meshicha; hair is the last thing to develop in a fetus, so the last generation completes Klal Yisroel.

title.en: Shimshon's revenge and the Palestinians

summary.en: The Rav brings Shimshon's prayer 'zochreini na' and his wish to take revenge on the Plishtim even at the cost of his life. He explains that the Palestinians are named after the Plishtim, and a name defines a thing, so Shimshon's war against them continues.

title.en: Yaakov's prayer and joining Shimshon's tefilah

summary.en: The Rav explains that Yaakov saw in Shimshon the soul that is the root of the generation of ikvesa d'meshicha and prayed for them 'lishuascha kivisi Hashem'. He recalls Shimshon's destruction of Aza, contrasts it with today, and calls on the listeners to daven together with Shimshon for revenge and for Eretz Yisroel and Yerushalayim to be for Jews.

title.en: Tefilah and a niggun

summary.en: A short prayer that the tefilah be accepted, followed by chanting of 'zochreinu' and a long stretch of singing, including a niggun attributed to the Skulener Rebbe.

title.en: Shimon HaTzaddik, remnant of the Knesses HaGedolah

summary.en: The Rav mentions that Shimon HaTzaddik prevented Alexander from destroying Yerushalayim, and explains that being one of the 'remnants' of the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah is like the shirayim of a Rebbe that connect people to him. Shimon HaTzaddik is the first named in the chain of the Oral Torah after Moshe and opened the era of the Tanna'im.

catalogTitle: קבר רחל - להתפלל על גאולת רחל וירושלים בחינתה. מערת המכפלה

oneLiner.en: Speaking at Kever Rochel and at the Me'aras HaMachpelah, the Rav calls for prayer for the redemption of Rochel and Yerushalayim, now surrounded by the 'uncircumcised and impure', and for the strength of Avraham Avinu's emunah, to stand alone against the whole world.

abstract.en: The Rav opens by thanking Hashem for the merit of davening Maariv at Kever Rochel. Rochel, he explains, is the aspect of Malchus, Shabbos, the Beis HaMikdash and Yerushalayim, which is why Tikkun Rochel at Tikkun Chatzos mourns Yerushalayim. He connects Rochel's words at Yosef's birth, 'Hashem has taken away my disgrace', to the disgrace of orlah, Esav who was never circumcised against Yosef who was born circumcised. He tells the Midrash of the maiden who fled the corruption before the Flood on an angel's wing and became the mazal of Elul, and urges grabbing Elul's opportunities. From the haftorah of Nachamu he describes Rochel and Yerushalayim surrounded by Yishmael, 'arel v'tamei', and calls for prayer for their redemption. At the Me'aras HaMachpelah he speaks of Avraham, one against the world, and Kalev, one against the spies, and asks for strength in today's tests of emunah. He closes with Tu B'Av, the coming joy of chassan and kallah, and accepting emunah.

en: Rochel is the aspect of Malchus, Shabbos, the Beis HaMikdash and Yerushalayim; Tikkun Rochel at Tikkun Chatzos is the mourning over Yerushalayim.
Elul is a month that can be 'grabbed', as the maiden and Yaakov grabbed it, and every Jew should seize its opportunities for Torah, mitzvos and chesed.
Kever Rochel, like Yerushalayim, the root of Rochel, is now surrounded by Yishmael, the 'arel v'tamei', and one must pray for Mother Rochel to be freed from them.
Like Avraham against the whole world and Kalev against the spies, an upright Jew today must hold to holy views even when he stands alone.
All prayers pass through the place of the Avos, which is why Shemoneh Esrei opens with 'the G-d of Avraham, the G-d of Yitzchak, the G-d of Yaakov'; there one should pray for emunah.
Tu B'Av begins the joy of the union of Hashem with Knesses Yisrael, like chassan and kallah, which will be complete when Mashiach comes.

He calls for prayer for Mother Rochel and ends with the pesukim of Rochel weeping for her children and their return.
