Such a person must daven longer, and his tears are tears of joy, like a parent and child reunited.

title.en: Every day and every person has a mission

summary.en: The Rav teaches that the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah set davening so that each day brings new light and its own tikkun, bringing Avraham 'ba bayamim', Hillel's 'if not now, when' and 'hamechadesh b'tuvo'. Every person comes for one moment of trial, like Moshe Rabbeinu for Matan Torah and Yosef, who became Yosef HaTzaddik through his test, so one must always be ready.

title.en: Preparing for great days and for Mashiach

summary.en: The Rav says great days are coming, Adar and especially Nisan, that things are stirring in the world, and that one must prepare a garment for Mashiach woven of Torah, mitzvos and tefillah. He ends with a brachah that all merit to greet Mashiach unashamed; a niggun and unclear talk follow.

oneLiner.en: The Rav tells bachurim that in the confusion of the final generation before Moshiach the main test is emunah, and, from Malachi's last prophecy, that those who fear Hashem must gather and strengthen one another.

abstract.en: The Rav opens by saying that we stand in ikvesa d'meshicha, the 'heel' of the generations before Moshiach, facing a test like Avraham Avinu's last one, where the Satan argued convincingly and Avraham did not listen. Every soul was sent down from heaven on a mission, and he reads the first chapter of Mesilas Yesharim: man was created to delight in Hashem, and this world is only a corridor to the next. No one finds real happiness here, and a soul greater than the angels was not given for eating and drinking. The main test now is emunah, and he tells of the Slonimer Rebbe, the talmidim of the Ba'al Shem Tov and the Ba'al Shem Tov himself. From the end of Malachi he shows that people will say serving Hashem does not pay, and the answer is that yirei Hashem speak to one another and strengthen each other. He ends with the Shabbos seudos, shalosh seudos and melave malka.

en: We are in the last stretch of ikvesa d'meshicha, and its test resembles Avraham Avinu's last test: not listening to the Satan even when his argument seems to make sense.
Following Mesilas Yesharim ch. 1, the Rav teaches that man was created to delight in Hashem, and this world is only a corridor to the World to Come.
In the final period of galus the main test is emunah, as the passuk says, 'tzaddik be'emunaso yichyeh'.
Malachi, the last prophet, foretells that people will say serving Hashem does not pay, and gives the answer: those who fear Hashem speak to one another and strengthen each other.
The three Shabbos seudos rise in greatness like the three tefillos, and melave malka, Dovid HaMelech's seudah, corresponds to chatzos and draws the holiness of Shabbos into the week.

summary.en: The Rav describes the soul singing with the angels in heaven before it was sent down on a mission, and reads the opening of Mesilas Yesharim: the foundation of chassidus is knowing one's obligation in the world, that man was created to delight in Hashem, that this world is a corridor to the next, and that life here is one long battle.

title.en: No true happiness in this world

summary.en: Continuing Mesilas Yesharim, the Rav says no one with sense can believe man was created for this world: even the richest and most powerful are full of troubles, competition and jealousy, and a soul greater than the angels was not needed for eating and playing. He then praises Mesilas Yesharim as a simple-looking sefer full of hidden depth.

title.en: Emunah as the test, and the Ba'al Shem Tov's talmidim

summary.en: The Rav says the main test before Moshiach is emunah, and that davening must be elevated. He tells of the Slonimer Rebbe sensing a problem that a learned man explained away, asks how the Ba'al Shem Tov's talmidim could surpass the Amoraim, and brings the Satmar Rav's answer that they were souls of prophets sent as an exception to save the world.

title.en: Stories of the Ba'al Shem Tov

summary.en: The Rav retells the Ruzhiner's story of how the Maggid trembled uncontrollably when he touched the Ba'al Shem Tov's garment during tefilas geshem, and how the Ba'al Shem Tov could only attend to worldly questions in the washroom, since his mind was always in heaven. He adds that the Ba'al Shem Tov's teacher was Achiya HaShiloni.

title.en: Malachi: 'serving Hashem does not pay'

summary.en: The Rav explains that Malachi, the last prophet, speaks to the last generation about how to cross the sea of galus. He reads Malachi's closing words and the complaint of the people that serving Hashem is futile and the wicked prosper, and tells of bachurim at a yeshiva lunch table who said the same.

title.en: 'Az nidberu yirei Hashem': strengthening one another

summary.en: The Rav explains Malachi's answer for that time: those who fear Hashem gather and speak to one another to strengthen their emunah, Hashem listens and writes every word in a book of remembrance, and at the geulah everyone will see the difference between the tzaddik and the rasha.

title.en: Middos, shalosh seudos and melave malka

summary.en: The Rav explains why he agreed to meet the bachurim on Motzaei Shabbos for words of chizuk, stresses good middos, and compares the three Shabbos seudos to the three tefillos, each greater than the one before. Melave malka, Dovid HaMelech's seudah, corresponds to chatzos and brings Shabbos into the week; he closes with a brachah.

catalogTitle: חסידות -- עיקרים וטפלים

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that holding on to emunah is an essence of Chassidus, that mockery is its opposite, and traces through history how every attempt to run away from the Ribono shel Olam failed, until the Ba'al Shem Tov revived the simple Jews.

abstract.en: The Rav opens by saying that Chassidus is misunderstood today: it has roots and branches, and among its roots are seeking the truth and holding on to emunah, swimming against the current. Avraham Avinu dug wells of emunah, and the Plishtim stopped them up. A sefer teaches that the opposite of emunah is mockery, and the Rav shows with a story of a boy who laughed at the Livyasan how one joke dismisses a hundred rebukes. That was how the Plishtim blocked Avraham's wells. He then follows the pattern through history: Mitzrayim, the exile, Yechezkel's warning that Jews cannot leave Hashem, the Haskalah in Germany, and Zionism, each meant to solve the Jews' troubles and each making them worse, illustrated with a parable of the animals' court. Jews kept their emunah through every persecution; after Shabsai Tzvi the Ba'al Shem Tov, a neshamah beyond his generation, raised up the simple Jews. He closes with stories of tzaddikim's sensitivity and of a chaburah that revived its listeners.

en: The Rav says Chassidus is misunderstood today; among its great roots are seeking and knowing the truth and holding on to emunah.
Mockery is the opposite of emunah: one joke can dismiss a hundred rebukes, without any logic or argument.
The Plishtim stopped up Avraham Avinu's wells of emunah by mocking his greatness, and Yitzchak had to dig them again.
Every attempt to escape the Ribono shel Olam, from the exile in Yechezkel's time to the Haskalah and Zionism, failed and brought the Jews worse troubles.
Through every persecution Jews gave their lives for kiddush Hashem because they held on to emunah.
After the fall caused by Shabsai Tzvi, Hashem sent the Ba'al Shem Tov, who raised up the simple Jews and showed them how precious they are to Hashem.

summary.en: The Rav tells of a boy who mocked his teacher's words about the Livyasan, and explains how one joke dismisses a hundred rebukes. This was the Plishtim's way of stopping up Avraham's wells; he follows the pattern through Mitzrayim, Matan Torah and the exile, where Yechezkel warned that Jews cannot leave Hashem.

title.en: Haskalah, Zionism and the hope to end antisemitism

summary.en: The Rav describes the Haskalah in Germany, which promised that becoming like the gentiles would end antisemitism and instead led to the churban, and the Zionist idea of a homeland, first Uganda and then Eretz Yisroel. He notes that tzaddikim had first urged settling Eretz Yisroel, but refused to partner with the free Zionists.

title.en: The state and the parable of the sheep

summary.en: The Rav says the Zionists succeeded beyond expectations, yet antisemitism became far worse, and the nations condemn the Jews for what every nation has done. He brings a vort on the last passuk of Tehillim 119 with a parable of the animals' court that excused the bear and the wolf and condemned the sheep, and concludes that nothing helps without the Ribono shel Olam.

title.en: Mesirus nefesh in exile and the Ba'al Shem Tov

summary.en: The Rav lists the generations of martyrdom, from the Ten Martyrs to the Crusades, the Inquisition and the decrees of 1648-49, all for emunah. After Shabsai Tzvi led many astray, Hashem sent the Ba'al Shem Tov, who lifted up the simple Jews; the Rav describes him as a neshamah beyond his generation, as the Gra was among the later authorities.

title.en: Stories of tzaddikim and a reviving chaburah

summary.en: The Rav mentions that tzaddikim could sense forbidden food, and tells of the Belzer Rav at a tish who sensed that a crystal plate of grapes had not been toveled. He then recalls a Thursday chaburah in Williamsburg where stories of tzaddikim left the young men refreshed and eager to learn and daven.

catalogTitle: Pitfalls of Emunah

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that after Pesach, the Yom Tov of emunah, the Torah warns against the two things that damage emunah most, forbidden food and breaches of kedushah, and describes how the Satan in our generation floods the world with both.

abstract.en: The Rav opens by recalling that Pesach is the Yom Tov of emunah and that matzah, which the Zohar calls the food of emunah, makes emunah part of a Jew's body. The two sedras read right after Pesach, Shemini on forbidden foods and Acharei on arayos, deal with the two greatest damagers of emunah. Treif food clogs the heart, as the Gemara reads 'venitmeisem' as 'venitamtem', and takes away a person's taste in Yiddishkeit and Shabbos. In the days before Moshiach the Satan, fighting for his life, floods the market with treif and doubtful hechsherim. The Rav tells of the Skverer Rebbe's extreme care, the Rambam's answer to doubters of techiyas hameisim, and a tzaddik who found a kernel of wheat in his Pesach soup because he had not davened. He then turns to kedushas habris, describes the streets and media of today, and urges escaping the city, guarding the home, and keeping good company.

en: Pesach is the Yom Tov of emunah, and by eating matzah, the food of emunah, a Jew internalizes emunah into his very body.
The sedras after Pesach, Shemini and Acharei, address forbidden food and arayos because these two damage emunah more than anything else.
Forbidden food clogs the heart, so that a person loses his feeling and taste in Yiddishkeit and in Shabbos.
In the days before Moshiach the Satan, fighting for his life, floods the market with treif and unreliable hechsherim.
Care in kashrus is not enough on its own; a person must also daven to Hashem not to stumble.
The Satan of this generation has concentrated on breaching kedushah through the streets and the media, a test no earlier generation faced.

title.en: Matzah, the food of emunah

summary.en: The Rav recalls that Pesach is the Yom Tov of emunah and that eating matzah makes emunah part of a Jew's body. He then notes that the sedras after Pesach, Shemini and Acharei, deal with forbidden food and arayos, the two greatest damagers of emunah.

title.en: Treif food dulls the taste of Yiddishkeit

summary.en: The Rav contrasts Jews who taste the sweetness of Shabbos with bochurim who complain they feel nothing on Shabbos, and says they probably ate treif. He brings the Gemara that reads 'venitmeisem' as 'venitamtem': forbidden food clogs the heart.

title.en: The Satan floods the market with treif

summary.en: The Rav explains that in the days before Moshiach the Satan, sensing danger, fights with extra strength and floods the market with forbidden food. Before World War I no Jew ate treif; today ingredients are so complex and hechsherim so unreliable that hardly anyone can say he never ate treif.

title.en: The Skverer Rebbe and the Rambam's letter

summary.en: The Rav tells how the Skverer Rebbe refused freshly squeezed orange juice because his father never drank it, and baked his bread all year from wheat he had cut himself. He then brings the Rambam's letter answering people who doubted techiyas hameisim: they ask because they ate forbidden food.

title.en: Care and tefillah: the kernel in the soup

summary.en: The Rav urges care in kashrus together with tefillah not to stumble, and tells of a tzaddik who cleaned for a month yet found a kernel of wheat in his soup at the Seder. Through a dream question he learned it happened because he had not davened for a kosher Pesach, and how a bird dropped it down the chimney.

title.en: Kedushas habris and the streets of today

summary.en: Turning to the second damager, the Rav links Pesach and bris milah to Avraham Avinu, the root of emunah, and explains that bris milah is a lifelong mitzvah of guarding kedushah. He describes how today's streets, laws and media have made this test greater than in any generation, bringing the Medrash on 'goy naval' in Haazinu.

title.en: Practical guarding: city, home and friends

summary.en: The Rav sums up that emunah is ruined by forbidden food and breaches of kedushas habris, and urges whoever can to leave the city in summer and to keep radio, television and inciting literature out of the home. He stresses the influence of friends and brings the Rambam that one must move away from a bad neighborhood.

catalogTitle: מטרת החסידות: להחזיק פשוטי עם באמונה: שמירת הקדושה: ואיחוד לבבות

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that the Ba'al Shem Tov came to strengthen simple Jews in emunah, and that bachurim today must prepare for their tests through guarding kedushah and through love and unity among Jews despite their differences.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the Ba'al Shem Tov's main aim: to strengthen simple Jews in emunah. Emunah is precious today, he says, and nobody knows what tests lie ahead. He tells how the Ba'al Shem Tov crossed a river on his belt and lit an icicle like a candle through emunah alone, and how he planted emunah and yiras Shamayim in the world. Just as the Avos prepared their children for Mitzrayim, the Ba'al Shem Tov's talmidim prepared later generations. Our generation is very low, and our task is to stay pure where it seems impossible. Before Moshiach there will be great tests, and for us they are small ones: guarding the eyes and thoughts, as Yosef did. A second kelipah today is machlokes between groups of ehrliche Jews. Different paths come from different roots, as R' Zeira stayed R' Yehudah's talmid and Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel loved each other. Bachurim must love every Jew who serves Hashem.

en: The Rav says the Ba'al Shem Tov's main aim was to strengthen simple Jews, above all in emunah.
The Ba'al Shem Tov's wonders, crossing a river on his belt and lighting an icicle, came from emunah alone, not from holy names.
As the Avos prepared the Jews for galus Mitzrayim, the Ba'al Shem Tov and his talmidim prepared the later generations for their tests.
The great test before Moshiach is, for this generation, a matter of small things: not looking, not speaking lashon hara, guarding the eyes and thoughts.
Machlokes between ehrliche Jews over 'my Rebbe and your Rebbe' is a great kelipah of today and not what the Ba'al Shem Tov intended.
Just as every person's face is different, so are his opinions and his path; one may follow his own way and still love the other.

candidateTopics: the Ba'al Shem Tov and emunah

title.en: Emunah today and the Besht's river crossing

summary.en: The Rav returns to the Ba'al Shem Tov's aim of strengthening simple Jews in emunah, notes how many come to him today with questions of emunah, and says nobody knows what tests lie ahead. He tells how the Ba'al Shem Tov crossed a great river standing on his belt, through emunah alone.

title.en: The burning icicle and seeing the soul's root

summary.en: From Shivchei HaBesht the Rav tells how the Ba'al Shem Tov lit an icicle like a candle on a cold night, comparing it to Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa. He adds the Belzer Rav's saying that every ehrliche Jew in Germany came from the Ba'al Shem Tov, and how the Maggid could see a soul's root down to the earth Adam was made from.

title.en: Preparing the generations, and our low state

summary.en: The Rav compares the Besht's talmidim to the Avos, who prepared the Jews for Mitzrayim; the tests of Yosef and Sarah gave Jewish men and women the strength to stay pure. He describes today's impurity entering homes, brings the Midrash on 'b'goy naval', and the Satan's task with Iyov, to break the barrel but keep the wine, as the picture of our task.

title.en: The tests before Moshiach are small things

summary.en: The Rav tells what a tzaddik in Yerushalayim, Rabbi Eliyahu Roth, foretold about Russia and the year 2000, and stresses that nobody can know the time; one must be ready for every test. A test is when one doesn't know the outcome, like Avraham at the Akeidah, and for this generation the tests are small: not looking out of curiosity, not speaking lashon hara.

title.en: Kedushas einayim and pure thoughts

summary.en: The Rav explains that Chanukah's lights train the eyes, so that one merits 'ki ayin b'ayin yiru'. A stray thought is not a sin; keeping it is, as the Bnei Yissaschar writes. Yosef was called tzaddik for guarding himself; this middah is called yesod, and failing in it can cost a person his tzelem Elokim and his taste for Shabbos.

title.en: The kelipah of machlokes; each path has its root

summary.en: The Rav names a second kelipah, machlokes among ehrliche Jews over 'my Rebbe, your Rebbe', brings the Divrei Chaim on the erev rav, and says the Besht never meant this. The Maggid's talmidim each went their own way, and minhagim differ even between cousins; he brings R' Zeira, who differed with R' Yehudah about Eretz Yisroel yet stayed his talmid.

title.en: Different faces, one love

summary.en: The Rav says pirud halevavos is among the great kelipos today and calls on bachurim to love every Jew who serves Hashem. As faces differ, so do opinions, like dollar bills from one plate versus people from Adam's mold; Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel loved each other. He mentions Emunas Yisroel taking good points from everywhere, the Besht's shared seudos, and sums up the two topics: shmiras hakedushah and unity.

catalogTitle: חשיבות העבודה בחושך

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that avodah done in a dark time like Teves, or in a dark place, is especially precious above, and then turns to how bachurim should go to sleep on time so as to rise fresh for avodah.

abstract.en: The Rav opens by urging that the light of Chanukah be carried into the dark month of Teves with hasmadah and bright tefillos, turning darkness to light. Citing Sefer Yetzirah, he shows that place, time and soul mirror each other: Yom Kippur, the Kohen Gadol and the Kodesh HaKodashim meet. The same holds for impurity, which has its place, its person and its time, Nittel, when the custom is not to learn. He brings the Gemara of Onkelos and the Bnei Yissaschar's explanation of the punishment of false wisdom. Yet Teves is also when great gems can be found in the depths, as in the parable of the pearl placed at the head of the king's crown. Following the Kedushas Levi, every time contains all times. The second half turns to rising early, kerias shema before sleep, sleep as avodah and a kind of techiyas hamesim, and going to sleep on time.

en: The Rav says that by bringing the light of Chanukah into Teves with hasmadah, Torah and bright tefillos, and with simcha, one turns the darkness into light.
Place, time and soul parallel one another; this holds for holiness and also for impurity, which has its place, its person and its time, Nittel.
Avodah done in a dark time or a dark place is valued in Heaven like the avodah of great tzaddikim, as the pearl from the dark depths was set at the head of the king's crown.
Following the Kedushas Levi, every time contains all times, so a Jew's avodah in Teves can awaken Pesach, Shavuos or Sukkos.
Sleep is part of avodas Hashem: in sleep the soul ascends and is strengthened, and sleep is a kind of techiyas hamesim from which a person rises a new creation.
The Rav says one must go to sleep early and on time, sleep as much as one truly needs to be alert, and not linger in bed past that.

title.en: Carrying Chanukah's light into Teves

summary.en: The Rav says that one who carries the light of Chanukah into Teves with hasmadah and bright tefillos turns darkness into light, and that the purpose is to go down to Mitzrayim and do great avodah there. He brings from Sefer Yetzirah that place, time and soul mirror one another, as Yom Kippur, the Kohen Gadol and the Kodesh HaKodashim meet.

title.en: Impurity's place, person and time: Nittel

summary.en: The Rav brings the Gemara of Onkelos and the Bnei Yissaschar's explanation of the punishment of wisdom cut off from holiness, and explains that just as there is a place where one may not learn, there is a time of impurity, Nittel, when the custom is not to learn. Yet in Teves, as one digging in the depths, a Jew who learns with effort and davens with fervor can achieve great things not possible in bright times.

title.en: The pearl at the head of the crown

summary.en: The Rav tells the parable of a king who made a crown from gems brought from every land, and a loyal servant who risked his life in the dark depths of the sea to bring a pearl, which the king set at the head of the crown though other stones were finer. He applies it to a simple Jew who serves Hashem with mesirus nefesh in hard times, whose avodah is set at the head of the crown like that of great tzaddikim.

title.en: Every time contains all times

summary.en: The Rav brings the Kedushas Levi that every time contains all times, so the akeidah could be both Pesach and Yom Kippur, and avodah in Teves can awaken any yom tov. Learning on a train or subway is also avodah from a place of darkness; he adds that bachurim davening in their yeshivos is also from Heaven, citing Rav Aharon of Karlin that one serves Hashem with whatever one can.

title.en: Going to sleep as part of avodah

summary.en: The Rav says one must rise early for Shacharis, and brings a tzaddik's answer to why the Shulchan Aruch, which opens with rising like a lion, gives no laws of going to sleep: one who lies down like a lion rises like a lion. He speaks of kerias shema before sleep driving away mazikin, the Arizal's ranking of the kerias shemas, and sleep as avodah in which the soul ascends and which is a kind of techiyas hamesim.

title.en: Enough sleep, and to bed on time

summary.en: The Rav says a person rises from sleep a new creation, tells of the Satmar Rav who did not sleep in a bed, and says that ordinary people cannot do such feats: without enough sleep one cannot learn. He brings the Gerrer Rebbe on eight hours for a bachur, Shlomo HaMelech's 'ad masai atzel tishkav' with a tzaddik's reading that laziness lies in going to bed late, and the Gur yeshiva's rule of going to sleep at one o'clock.

catalogTitle: The 50th Gate of קדושה is Opposed to the 50th Gate of טומאה

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that the fiftieth gate of tumah, apikorsus, stands opposite the fiftieth gate of kedushah, emunah, and that the doubts it sends before Mashiach must be ignored rather than argued with.

abstract.en: After a short warning about insects in food during the summer, the Rav turns to Shavuos, the fiftieth day. Hashem took the Jews out of Egypt from the forty-nine gates of tumah just before they fell into the fiftieth, and since everything in creation is balanced, the fifty gates of tumah stand opposite the fifty gates of kedushah. The first forty-nine are midos, each with a nation as its vessel, as he shows with chesed and gevurah and the dream of the Ohr HaChaim; the fiftieth is daas: in kedushah emunah, in tumah apikorsus, whose force is Amalek, numerically equal to safek. Citing the Ohr HaChaim that before Mashiach the Jews fall into this gate, he describes the doubts that torment even believing Jews and explains that they are not logical, so one must ignore them and drive them away, a fulfillment of lo sasuru. He closes with the story of Reb Mendel of Vitebsk and the mazikim.

en: The fifty gates of tumah stand opposite the fifty gates of kedushah, because Hashem made everything in balance.
The first forty-nine gates are midos; the fiftieth is daas: emunah in kedushah and apikorsus in tumah.
Before Mashiach the Jews fall into the fiftieth gate of tumah, and the Torah is what lets them hold on to emunah inside it.
Amalek is the force of the fiftieth gate of tumah; its purpose is to inject doubt in emunah, and Amalek is numerically equal to safek.
Thoughts of doubt are not logical and cannot be answered with logic; one must ignore them and not argue with them.
Driving such a thought away is itself the mitzvah of lo sasuru; the sin is only in giving it lodging in the mind.
The trial is temporary and has a limit; one who fights and stays with emunah comes out with emunah clearer and purer than before.

title.en: Insects in summer; the fiftieth gate

summary.en: The Rav warns about insects in food in the hot weather. He then turns to Shavuos: Hashem took the Jews out of the forty-nine gates of tumah before they fell into the fiftieth, and each day of Sefirah brings them into a gate of kedushah, with the fiftieth being emunah; since everything is balanced, fifty gates of tumah stand opposite fifty gates of kedushah.

title.en: The fiftieth gate is apikorsus

summary.en: The Rav explains that the forty-nine gates are midos while the fiftieth is daas: emunah in kedushah, apikorsus in tumah. He brings the Ohr HaChaim that before Mashiach the Jews will fall into the fiftieth gate; unlike in Egypt they now have the Torah to hold on to, and he says the world today is in that gate.

title.en: The seven nations and the midos

summary.en: The Rav explains that each bad midah has a nation as its vessel. Chesed is giving and gevurah is recoiling; in kedushah the right and the giver lead, as seen in dressing right first and in kiddushin, while in tumah the left dominates, as he shows from Esav and from the Ohr HaChaim's dream of two dogs. That is why the chesed of tumah is called Canaani, and he touches on Chiti for gevurah.

title.en: Amalek and the doubts of today

summary.en: The Rav identifies Amalek as the force of the fiftieth gate of tumah, whose purpose is to inject doubts in emunah. He describes how many believing Jews, even bnei Torah, suffer from such doubts and fight them, and how young men come to him crying, unable to sleep.

title.en: Doubts are not logical

summary.en: The Rav brings the Ruzhiner that before Mashiach simple emunah will be like climbing a slippery wall, and the Zohar on that period. He says even great tzaddikim had such doubts; they are not logical but like a bug, as in people who keep checking a locked door. One of the Erev Rav welcomes such thoughts, while a Jew from Har Sinai fights them; the Rav says not to argue with them, for it is like a fly in a spider web.

title.en: Ignore them: lo sasuru

summary.en: The Rav tells of a man who could not daven because of an image in his mind, and Rabbi Nachman of Breslov told him to ignore it. Driving such thoughts away is the mitzvah of lo sasuru, and the Rav gives a remez for it. The doubts are a temporary punishment with a limit, and one who fights them comes out with purer emunah.

title.en: Summary: emunah beyond understanding

summary.en: The Rav repeats and summarizes: the fiftieth gate of kedushah, reached on Shavuos, is emunah, which even Moshe Rabbeinu could not grasp, and its opposite is apikorsus, which is also beyond logic. He brings the Chovos HaLevavos's image of ink splashing into a poem, and explains that today, unlike pagan times, people believe in nothing, because this is the time of Amalek, numerically equal to safek.

title.en: A Jew from Sinai resists the doubts

summary.en: The Rav says every Jew who stood at Sinai would give his life for emunah, as whole communities did in the Crusades. The atmosphere is full of apikorsus, so such thoughts penetrate even believers, and he brings the Zohar praising one who holds on to emunah before Mashiach. A Jew from Sinai resents these thoughts while one of the Erev Rav welcomes them; again he says not to argue but to ignore them.

title.en: Reb Mendel of Vitebsk and the mazikim

summary.en: The Rav tells the story the Tzemach Tzedek related: a chassid of Reb Mendel of Vitebsk was taken by mazikim to a bris, warned by a captive woman not to eat, and told by his Rebbe to say they are nothing. The mazikim shrank away as he said it, and Ashmedai told him he had no power over him because his Rebbe's Torah was entirely for Heaven's sake.

catalogTitle: מודה אני - הכרת הטוב: נעגעל וואסער: נחיצות ראשית היום: שלא לשוח לפני התפילה

oneLiner.en: The Rav teaches that the first moments of the day, Modeh Ani, negel vasser and the time before davening, set the course of everything after them and must be given to Hashem.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with Modeh Ani: the whole avodah of a Jew is thanking Hashem, and one must train oneself to thank parents, teachers and friends, so that the first words of the morning are thanks, said even before negel vasser. He then explains negel vasser: man was created with all ten utterances of creation, and the ten fingers are the control knobs of the body and of the world, so washing them is like immersing in a mikvah and purifies one's share of creation. Each soul is sent to its generation to purify it. Since the beginning controls everything, as with Rosh Hashanah and the first of the dough, the first thought, word and act must be for Hashem, and one must not chatter before davening. A story of the Sanzer Rav shows that excuses come to those who want them. He praises learning several hours without a break, and closes on zerizus and on the newness of every moment.

en: The whole avodah of a Jew is thanking Hashem, and one must train oneself to thank people as well, sincerely and not as lip service.
Modeh Ani is said even before negel vasser, because thanking Hashem is too urgent to wait.
Washing the ten fingers, which correspond to the ten utterances of creation, purifies the whole body and one's share of the world, like immersion in a mikvah.
Because the beginning controls everything that follows, the first thought, word and act of the day must be devoted to Hashem.
One must hold oneself back from idle talk before davening; whoever wants excuses will find them.
Every day and every moment is new and carries an avodah that will never return.

title.en: Modeh Ani and the duty to thank

summary.en: The Rav warns that Modeh Ani said out of habit loses its meaning, explains that the whole avodah of a Jew is thanking Hashem, and urges thanking parents, teachers and friends. Thanks is so urgent that Modeh Ani comes even before negel vasser.

title.en: Negel vasser: the ten fingers as control knobs

summary.en: The Rav compares the fingers to the control knobs of a machine: man was made with all ten utterances of creation, and washing the ten fingers purifies the whole body. He brings that washing the hands is like immersing in a mikvah, and a nusach of Rabbi Mordechai of Chernobyl to wash forty times in place of mikvah.

title.en: Purifying one's share of creation and generation

summary.en: The Rav shows from the flood that man holds a share of all creation, and brings that washing negel vasser purifies the world. Each soul is sent to its generation with a mission to purify it, and he describes how negel vasser should be washed properly.

title.en: The beginning controls all; no talk before davening

summary.en: From Rosh Hashanah and the first of the dough the Rav teaches that the beginning controls everything, so the first thought, word and act must be for Hashem. He then speaks sharply against chatter before davening, in the mikvah or over coffee.

title.en: The Sanzer Rav and the moth-eaten bekeshe

summary.en: To show that one who wants excuses finds them, the Rav tells of a man in Sanz whose new silk bekeshe tore at every touch, and of the Sanzer Rav's answer. He concludes that one who is serious about his avodah will not find excuses.

title.en: Learning several hours without a break

summary.en: The Rav praises the custom of bochurim to learn several hours in a row without interruption, recalls Rav Aharon Kotler's words on the seventh hour, and explains that such learning trains the power of restraint against curiosity.

title.en: Zerizus and the newness of every moment

summary.en: Using the army as a mashal, the Rav calls for zerizus in the service of Hashem. He teaches that the soul is renewed every morning and that every moment has an avodah never seen before, and closes with the Chiddushei HaRim on 'if not now, when'.

catalogTitle: רוב התיקון בזמננו הוא ע”י תפילה בהשתפכות הנפש

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that in our weak generation the Beis HaMikdash is built through small avodos, and that the greatest tikun of our time is tefillah poured out with the heart, word by word and aloud.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the idea that Hashem created the world with flaws so that people would repair them, and that Klal Yisrael was chosen for this. He tells how the Sanzer Rav said the Beis HaMikdash was almost complete except for the paroches, and concludes that building outpaces destruction, so today only small parts remain. Earlier generations did great avodos; we are weaker, so small avodos are asked of us: coming to davening on time, not talking during learning, holding back a joke or lashon hara. With a mashal of a parrot before a king he shows how precious they are in heaven. Every avodah is a birur, and every tefillah is a different one. The greatest tikun of our time, revealed by the Arizal, is tefillah with hishtapchus hanefesh. He brings the Baal HaTanya's letter on davening slowly, word by word, with fixed baalei tefillah, explains why one davens aloud, and calls on the bachurim to daven together near the table.

en: Hashem created the world with imperfections so that people, and Klal Yisrael above all, would repair them.
The building of the Beis HaMikdash moves faster than its destruction, so in our time only small parts are left to complete.
Because our generations are weaker, Hashem asks small avodos of us, such as coming to davening on time, not talking during learning and not embarrassing a friend.
Every avodah is a birur, a refining of good from evil, and every day's tefillah accomplishes a different one.
The greatest tikun of our time, as the Arizal revealed, is through tefillah with hishtapchus hanefesh.
Davening aloud, word by word, arouses kavanah, and the Rav asks the bachurim to daven together near the table and strengthen one another.

candidateTopics: small avodos in a weak generation

title.en: A flawed world given to man to repair

summary.en: The Rav explains that Hashem created the world with flaws for people to repair, that more flaws came through Adam's sin and later aveiros, and that Klal Yisrael was chosen to bring light. Though the forces of evil seem to grow, he compares Hashem to a businessman who keeps up his business because he knows it profits.

title.en: The Sanzer Rav and the missing paroches

summary.en: The Rav tells how the Sanzer Rav said at his tish that the Beis HaMikdash was nearly finished except for the paroches, which he had sewn and reshaim had torn. From this he learns that building outpaces destruction, that after the great tzaddikim from Rabbi Akiva on made the large parts, only small pieces like screws remain for us.

title.en: Small avodos of a weak generation

summary.en: The Rav contrasts the great avodos of earlier generations, who fasted from Shabbos to Shabbos, with our weaker generations, and says small avodos are asked of us: coming to davening on time, not talking in learning, holding back a joke or lashon hara. With a mashal of a talking parrot brought before a king, he explains that these small deeds are precious in heaven and are the last screws of the Beis HaMikdash.

title.en: Every avodah and every tefillah a birur

summary.en: The Rav brings the Sefer HaChinuch on milah: Hashem left man imperfect so he would perfect himself, and so every avodah is a birur that repairs the world. Each tefillah is a different birur, since the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah, prophets among them, composed it with ruach hakodesh so that each day accomplishes something else; he urges using the coming weeks for takanos in learning and davening.

title.en: The tikun of our time: tefillah with hishtapchus hanefesh

summary.en: After a word on negel vasser repairing oneself and the world, the Rav says the greatest tikun of our time, revealed by the Arizal, is tefillah. He tells how their beis medrash arose with siyata dishmaya and how the Skverer Rebbe encouraged its way of tefillah, and describes two ways of hishtapchus hanefesh: holding on to each word, or davening fast, the second only for the fully pure. He brings the Chasam Sofer quoting the Baal Shem Tov that each word of davening is a heichal one must not be pushed out of.

title.en: The Baal HaTanya's letter on davening

summary.en: The Rav reads from a letter of the Baal HaTanya, printed in the Tanya and hung in his shtiblach, complaining that in some places people do not let davening go at its proper pace. Along the way he brings the Gemara that one who prolongs his tefillah has his days lengthened, with a story of a bachur who answered a friend with it.

title.en: Fixed baalei tefillah and davening aloud

summary.en: The Rav explains the Baal HaTanya's takanah of fixed baalei tefillah who daven word by word at a moderate pace and aloud, since a raised voice arouses kavanah. He answers those who ask why one should shout with Yom Kippur, tells of a Galitzianer chassid who was surprised by the chassidim of Kotzk, and adds that a person naturally raises his voice when he truly means something.

title.en: A call to daven together near the table

summary.en: The Rav compares the shout at a home run to davening one means, points to the danger to Klal Yisrael in Eretz Yisrael that calls for tefillos, and recalls a group of bachurim who davened aloud around the baal tefillah and left a gap. Citing the first halacha of the Shulchan Aruch not to be ashamed before mockers, he asks the bachurim to daven aloud near the table, strengthen each other and so bring the geulah.
